# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

## Task: the external implementer, so any coding agent can be measured by the Proving Ground

Today `packages/improvement/environment-runner` creates one harness agent per cell (`ctx.agents.create`, `installModelSelection`) and drives its turns through the LLM seam. This slice adds a second way to implement a cell: delegating the task to an out-of-process coding agent through the subagent seam (`packages/subagent/subagent`: `ctx.subagents.start(name, request)` with `SubagentStartRequest { prompt, parent, signal, label?, agentOptions?, outputSchema? }` and the providers `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-acp`, `subagent-dsh-sdk`, plus the in-process `subagent-fork-in-process` and `subagent-spawn-in-process`), while the runner keeps every measurement it owns: the `environment/run` stamp, the budget caps, the standard authored before the work, the reservation under the read barrier, the checks it executes itself, `verification/run` with `executor: 'runner'`, tamper digests, certificates, directives as follow-ups, and the trajectory and facts folds. Read the runner whole, the subagent seam's README and types, `subagent-claude-code`'s README (how it resolves `claude`, its `env` config, how it derives the child's cwd from the parent agent), the in-process providers (how they inherit the parent's route, which the mock route serves keylessly), the read-barrier note's rule that out-of-process subagent providers record `unenforced` and refuse to start under a `process` or `host` claim, and the Village note's Proving Ground and publication rules. Do NOT touch `packages/governance/**`, `packages/improvement/program/**`, `packages/improvement/observatory/**`, or `packages/verification/tool-standard-author/**`; read them only.

Write first a bilingual Agent Note `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md` (+ `.zh.md`, pairing recorded) with the required sections, then implement:

1. **The request field**: `EnvironmentRunRequest.implementer?: { kind: 'route' } | { kind: 'subagent', provider: string, label?: string }`, defaulted to `{ kind: 'route' }` in the runner's explicit resolve step; validated against the composed subagent providers at run time (`ENVIRONMENT_RUN_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE` naming the provider when `ctx.subagents` is absent or has no provider by that name); refused for a deployment `isolation` above `none` when the provider is out-of-process, with a pinned error, because the read-barrier census cannot confine it (an in-process provider inherits the parent's composition and may keep the deployment's isolation).
2. **The delegated attempt loop**: for `kind: 'subagent'` the runner still creates the cell agent and session as today (stamp, caps, standard, reservation, `agent/session-start`), but instead of driving the cell agent's turns it starts one child run per attempt through `ctx.subagents.start(provider, { prompt: [task text on the first attempt, the directive follow-up text on later ones], parent: cellAgent, signal, label })`, whose working directory is the cell workspace (verify how the provider derives it from the parent agent's session cwd and set the cell agent's cwd accordingly; if a provider needs an explicit cwd, pass it the way its README documents), awaits the run's result, and appends a durable `environment/delegation { attempt, provider, runId, stopReason, structured?, usage? }` event to the cell session (declared in `src/types.ts` by `SessionEventMap` merging, catalog regenerated), then validates exactly as today: tamper digest, check execution by the runner, `recordRun` with `executor: 'runner'`, certificate or directive. The census recorded for the cell names the provider through the existing `unenforced`/`denied-at-executor` vocabulary as the read-barrier slice 5 specified for out-of-process providers; say in the note what the certificate of a delegated cell proves (the runner ran the checks on the tree the external agent left) and what it does not (no model-visible history of the implementer lives in our log, so the trajectory carries no steps and is not training data).
3. **Fleet and shifts** forward an optional `implementer` from the plan to every cell (`FleetPlan.implementer?`, `ShiftDistrictConfig.plan.implementer?`, included in the shift digest), with unit coverage; `LeaderboardRow` and the scorekeeper facts gain `implementer` (`route` or the provider name, read from the stamp: put `implementer` on `EnvironmentRunStamp` so it is durable and partitions rows; rows never merge implementers). The observatory publishes the column as it does the others (touch `packages/improvement/observatory` only for the row field and its rendering; keep its tests green).
4. **Tests**: unit specs at 100% per-file coverage over a stubbed subagent service (delegation per attempt, the follow-up prompt carrying the directive, the durable event, refusal without the provider, refusal above `none` for out-of-process, the route default); a Loader-booted e2e under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/external-implementer/` using the in-process `spawn-in-process` (or `fork-in-process`, whichever inherits the parent route) subagent provider over the mock route so it runs keylessly, proving a delegated cell certifies on `smoke:round-trip`, fails on `smoke:unsatisfiable` with two attempts and one delegation event per attempt, and that the stamp, facts, and leaderboard carry `implementer`; plus a second composition `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml` composing `subagent-claude-code` as the provider with the runner, fleet, budget policy (`maxTotalTokens: 5000000`, `maxWallMs: 600000`), persistence, checkpoint policy, scorekeeper, observatory, and trajectories, plus a driver that runs one fleet plan of the two smoke environments with `implementer: { kind: 'subagent', provider: 'claude-code' }` and prints the report, facts, and the observatory document; its e2e is a **with-key style** test that self-skips unless `DSH_E2E_CLAUDE_CODE=1` is set (state in its docstring that it drives the real Claude Code CLI on the host's own authentication and is run by hand), following how the real-API e2e tests self-skip in `docs/testing.md`. Do not run the real Claude Code e2e yourself unless `claude -p "ok"` works in your worktree shell; if it does, run it once and report the report's certified counts.
5. **Docs**: README pairs (runner: the two implementer kinds, what a delegated certificate proves, the isolation rule; fleet, shifts, scorekeeper, observatory: the new field), `docs/subsystems/improvement.md` (+ ZH, type-equiv in sync), catalogs regenerated (`gen-cordis-catalog`, `gen-config-catalog`, `gen-doc-graphs`, `gen-persistence-catalog`) with Chinese twins mirrored and pairing re-recorded, the Village note's Proving Ground paragraph gaining one sentence that external coding agents run as implementers under the same certificates at `isolation: none` (EN + ZH), and `verify-village-composition` unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Requires every same-repository dependency chain to use GitHub's official stacked-PR feature before landing so GitHub owns stack-wide rules, CI, ordering, retargeting, and merge state.

## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web, developer, and research search. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated documentation sites and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. All tools are read-only and return ranked results.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Hugging_Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:

alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.

142	/**

144	 * as the second word of the check command line, so the path must need no shell
145	 * quoting: quoting is dialect-specific and the runner does not know the composed
146	 * shell's dialect.

150	/** Key the check-owned digest records the reservation's tree under. */
151	const RESERVATION_KEY = '<reservation>'

153	/** Subdirectory of a reservation holding one directory per check. */

155	/** File inside a check's reserved directory holding its run instruction. */

164	/**
165	 * Reservation subdirectory holding the reference program of an environment
166	 * that declares `task.reference`. It sits inside the reservation, so the
167	 * check-owned digest already covers it and an implementer is denied it by the
168	 * same rule that denies the check scripts beside it.

170	export const REFERENCE_DIR = 'reference'

172	/**
173	 * File inside {@link REFERENCE_DIR} the validator's instrument sources to run
174	 * the reference, mirroring the `run` file of a reserved check. A fixed name
175	 * rather than a configured one: it is the convention an environment author and
176	 * the instrument agree on, not a deployment choice.

178	export const REFERENCE_ENTRY = 'run'

180	/** A check id usable as one path segment of its reserved directory. */
181	const SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/

183	/**
184	 * Absolute path of one check's reserved directory, which holds its run script
185	 * and its case bodies. A check id that is not a single path segment, and a
186	 * script path the check command line cannot carry unquoted, are both refused.
187	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation the barrier minted for this run.
188	 * @param checkId - the check's id, used verbatim as the directory's name.
189	 * @returns the absolute check directory.
190	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when the id or the resulting path is unusable.
191	 */
192	function checkDirectory(runDirectory: string, checkId: string): string {
193	  if (!SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT.test(checkId)) {
194	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`check "${checkId}" cannot name a reserved script file`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
195	  }
196	  const directory = join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR, checkId)
197	  if (!UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD.test(join(directory, RUN_FILE))) {
198	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`reserved check script "${join(directory, RUN_FILE)}" contains characters the check command line cannot carry unquoted`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
199	  }
200	  return directory
201	}

203	/** Directory test that treats a missing or unreadable path as no directory. */
204	async function isDirectory(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
205	  try {
206	    return (await stat(path)).isDirectory()
207	  } catch {
208	    // stat rejects for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the caller named no usable directory.
209	    return false
210	  }
211	}

213	/** What one check-owned path digests to when nothing is there to read. */
214	const ABSENT_DIGEST = 'absent'
215	
216	/**
217	 * SHA-256 over one check-owned path: its tree when a directory, its bytes when
218	 * a file, and {@link ABSENT_DIGEST} when it is gone. Deleting a declared path
219	 * is as much a change to the check-owned set as rewriting it.
220	 * @param path - absolute path to digest.
221	 * @returns the digest, or the absent marker.
222	 */
223	async function hashCheckOwnedPath(path: string): Promise<string> {
224	  if (await isDirectory(path)) return hashWorkspaceTree(path)
225	  try {
226	    return createHash('sha256').update(await readFile(path)).digest('hex')
227	  } catch {
228	    // readFile rejects for a missing or unreadable path; either way the run
229	    // cannot read what the fixture supplied, which is the change to record.
230	    return ABSENT_DIGEST
231	  }
232	}

234	/**
235	 * SHA-256 over the whole check-owned set: the validator's reserved directory,
236	 * when a barrier minted one, and every path the environment declared immutable,
237	 * each keyed by the name it is declared under.
238	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory, which immutable paths are relative to.
239	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
240	 * @param immutable - the environment's declared immutable paths.
241	 * @returns one digest over the whole set.
242	 */
243	async function hashCheckOwned(
244	  workspace: string,
245	  runDirectory: string | undefined,
246	  immutable: readonly string[],
247	): Promise<string> {
248	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
249	  if (runDirectory !== undefined) {
250	    hash.update(RESERVATION_KEY).update('\0').update(await hashWorkspaceTree(runDirectory)).update('\0')
251	  }
252	  for (const path of immutable) {
253	    hash.update(path).update('\0').update(await hashCheckOwnedPath(join(workspace, path))).update('\0')
254	  }
255	  return hash.digest('hex')
256	}

258	/**
259	 * Copy the task's reference tree beneath one reservation, so the validator
260	 * runs the reference from a directory the barrier denies every implementer.
261	 * @param task - the task, supplying the fixture and its reference directory.
262	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation to stock.
263	 */
264	async function copyReference(task: EnvironmentTask, runDirectory: string): Promise<void> {
265	  // A registered reference always resolves inside its task's fixture.
266	  if (task.reference === undefined) return
267	  await cp(join(task.fixture as string, task.reference), join(runDirectory, REFERENCE_DIR), { recursive: true })

270	/**
271	 * Overlay the task fixture and drop the reference tree from the copy. The
272	 * reference belongs to the validator: it lives under the fixture so the
273	 * environment's content hashes cover it, and it is removed here so no overlay
274	 * ever leaves it where the implementer works.
275	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory.
276	 * @param task - the task, supplying the fixture and any reference.
277	 */
278	async function overlayFixture(workspace: string, task: EnvironmentTask): Promise<void> {
279	  if (task.fixture === undefined) return
280	  await cp(task.fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
281	  if (task.reference !== undefined) await rm(join(workspace, task.reference), { recursive: true, force: true })

284	/**
285	 * Reject a workspace or fixture that is not an existing absolute directory,
286	 * then overlay the fixture and return its digest.
287	 * @returns the fixture digest, or `undefined` for a task without a fixture.
288	 */
289	async function prepareWorkspace(workspace: string, task: EnvironmentTask): Promise<string | undefined> {
290	  if (!isAbsolute(workspace) || !await isDirectory(workspace)) {
291	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`workspace "${workspace}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE')
292	  }
293	  const fixture = task.fixture
294	  if (fixture === undefined) return undefined
295	  if (!isAbsolute(fixture) || !await isDirectory(fixture)) {
296	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`fixture "${fixture}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE')

298	  await overlayFixture(workspace, task)
299	  return hashWorkspaceTree(fixture)

303	 * Overlay the fixture again so implementer edits to validator-owned files do

306	 * @param task - the task, supplying the fixture and any reference.

314	/**
315	 * Write the attempt's standard snapshot, one run script per active check, and
316	 * each cased check's bodies into the reservation, so what the checks execute
317	 * and what they measure live where the implementer cannot read them. The whole
318	 * reservation is inside the check-owned digest, which is what covers the case
319	 * bodies against tampering.
320	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
321	 * @param standard - the standard this attempt measures.
322	 * @param bodies - case bodies per check id, from the environment definition.
323	 * @returns the script path per check id; empty without a reservation.
324	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when a check id cannot name a script file.
325	 */
326	async function materializeChecks(
327	  runDirectory: string | undefined,
328	  standard: StandardView,
329	  bodies: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly CheckCase[]>,
330	): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
331	  const scripts = new Map<string, string>()
332	  if (runDirectory === undefined) return scripts
333	  await mkdir(join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
334	  await writeFile(join(runDirectory, STANDARD_FILE), `${JSON.stringify(standard, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
335	  for (const check of standard.checks) {
336	    const directory = checkDirectory(runDirectory, check.id)
337	    await mkdir(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
338	    const script = join(directory, RUN_FILE)
339	    await writeFile(script, `${check.run}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
340	    const cases = bodies.get(check.id)
341	    if (cases !== undefined) {
342	      await writeFile(
343	        join(directory, CASES_FILE),
344	        cases.map(body => `${JSON.stringify(body)}\n`).join(''),
345	        { mode: 0o600 },
346	      )
347	    }
348	    scripts.set(check.id, script)
349	  }
350	  return scripts
351	}

353	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
354	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
355	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted
356	}

358	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
359	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
360	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
361	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
362	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
363	  const marker = '\n…'
364	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
365	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
366	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
367	}
368	
369	/** How one command ended, as the evidence states it. */
370	function exitLine(result: ShellRunResult): string {
371	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
372	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
373	  return `${exit}${cause}`
374	}
375	
376	/** The captured output tails of one command, omitting an empty stream. */
377	function outputLines(result: ShellRunResult): string[] {
378	  const lines: string[] = []
379	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
380	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
381	  return lines
382	}
383	
384	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
385	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
386	  return bound([exitLine(result), ...outputLines(result)].join('\n'), maxChars)
387	}

389	/** How the candidate ended one case, as the directive clusters it. */
390	function exitClassOf(result: ShellRunResult): CaseExitClass {
391	  if (result.timedOut) return 'timeout'
392	  if (result.exitCode === null) return 'signal'
393	  return result.exitCode === 0 ? 'zero' : 'nonzero'
394	}

397	const EXIT_PHRASE: Readonly<Record<CaseExitClass, string>> = {
398	  zero: 'the program exited 0',
399	  nonzero: 'the program exited non-zero',
400	  signal: 'the program was terminated by a signal',
401	  timeout: 'the program exceeded the case timeout',
402	}

422	/** Render one cased check's evidence: the tally, then each named failed case with its captured output. */
423	function casedEvidenceOf(run: CasedCheckRun, named: readonly CaseFailure[], maxChars: number): string {
424	  const lines = [`cases: ${run.passed} of ${run.total} passed (weight ${run.weightPassed} of ${run.weightTotal})`]
425	  for (const failure of named) {
426	    lines.push(`case "${failure.id}" differed on ${failure.channels.join(', ')}; ${exitLine(failure.result)}`)

432	/**
433	 * Whether one captured stream disagrees with its expected digest. A truncated
434	 * stream disagrees whatever it holds: the executor dropped bytes the digest
435	 * covers, so the comparison cannot be made.
436	 */
437	function streamMismatch(
438	  stream: ShellRunResult['stdout'],
439	  expected: string | undefined,
440	  normalizers: readonly CheckCaseNormalizer[],
441	): boolean {
442	  return stream.truncated || caseChannelDigest(Buffer.from(stream.text, 'utf8'), normalizers) !== expected
443	}

445	/**
446	 * The configured channels of one case whose observed value disagrees with the
447	 * case's expected digest, in the canonical channel order the log records.
448	 * @param body - the case that ran.
449	 * @param result - what the candidate produced.
450	 * @param scope - the absolute `treeScope` directory, absent for a check that declares none.
451	 * @returns the mismatching channels; empty when the case passed.
452	 */
453	async function caseMismatches(
454	  body: CheckCase,
455	  result: ShellRunResult,
456	  scope: string | undefined,
457	): Promise<CheckCaseChannel[]> {
458	  const { normalizers } = body.comparator
459	  const mismatched = new Set<CheckCaseChannel>()
460	  for (const channel of body.comparator.channels) {
461	    switch (channel) {
462	      case 'exit':
463	        if (result.exitCode !== body.expected.exitCode) mismatched.add(channel)
464	        break
465	      case 'stdout':
466	        if (streamMismatch(result.stdout, body.expected.stdoutSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
467	        break
468	      case 'stderr':
469	        if (streamMismatch(result.stderr, body.expected.stderrSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
470	        break
471	      case 'tree':
472	        // Authoring requires a treeScope for every check whose cases compare the tree.
473	        if (await hashWorkspaceTree(scope as string, normalizers) !== body.expected.treeSha256) mismatched.add(channel)
474	        break
475	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
476	      default:
477	        return assertNever(channel)
478	    }
479	  }
480	  return CHECK_CASE_CHANNELS.filter(channel => mismatched.has(channel))
481	}

501	  /** Exit, signal, timeout, and the captured `stdout` and `stderr` of the command. */

507	/**
508	 * Run one case and capture all four channels: empty the case's `treeScope`,
509	 * stage its files, append its `argv` to the command, and feed its `stdin`.
510	 * Both executors of a case go through here — the runner measuring a candidate
511	 * and the instrument recording a reference — so what a case means is one
512	 * procedure rather than two that can drift.
513	 * @param shell - the composed shell executor.
514	 * @param execution - the resolved command, workspace, input, and bounds.
515	 * @returns the command's result and the tree scope it left.
516	 */
517	export async function captureCase(shell: Context['shell'], execution: CaseExecution): Promise<CaseCapture> {
518	  const scope = execution.treeScope === undefined ? undefined : join(execution.workspace, execution.treeScope)
519	  if (scope !== undefined) {
520	    await rm(scope, { recursive: true, force: true })
521	    await mkdir(scope, { recursive: true })
522	  }
523	  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(execution.input.files ?? {})) {
524	    const staged = join(execution.workspace, path)
525	    await mkdir(dirname(staged), { recursive: true })
526	    await writeFile(staged, content)
527	  }
528	  const stdin = execution.input.stdin
529	  const result = await shell.run(shell.resolve({
530	    command: [execution.command, ...execution.input.argv].join(' '),
531	    workdir: execution.workspace,
532	    timeoutMs: execution.timeoutMs,
533	    signal: execution.signal,
534	    ...stdin === undefined ? {} : { stdin },
535	  }))
536	  return { result, ...scope === undefined ? {} : { scope } }
537	}

539	/**
540	 * The expected digests one capture establishes for a comparator's configured
541	 * channels, which is what {@link caseMismatches} later compares a candidate
542	 * against. A truncated compared stream yields no digest for that channel: the
543	 * executor dropped bytes the digest would cover, so nothing could ever match it.
544	 * @param capture - what the reference produced for the case.
545	 * @param comparator - the channels compared and the normalizers applied first.
546	 * @returns the expectation, holding one value per configured channel that could be digested.
547	 */
548	export async function caseExpectation(
549	  capture: CaseCapture,
550	  comparator: CheckCaseComparator,
551	): Promise<CheckCaseExpectation> {
552	  const { normalizers } = comparator
553	  const { result } = capture
554	  const digest = (stream: ShellRunResult['stdout']): Record<string, never> | { sha256: string } => (
555	    stream.truncated ? {} : { sha256: caseChannelDigest(Buffer.from(stream.text, 'utf8'), normalizers) }
556	  )
557	  let expectation: CheckCaseExpectation = {}
558	  for (const channel of comparator.channels) {
559	    switch (channel) {
560	      case 'exit':
561	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...result.exitCode === null ? {} : { exitCode: result.exitCode } }
562	        break
563	      case 'stdout': {
564	        const value = digest(result.stdout)
565	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...'sha256' in value ? { stdoutSha256: value.sha256 } : {} }
566	        break
567	      }
568	      case 'stderr': {
569	        const value = digest(result.stderr)
570	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...'sha256' in value ? { stderrSha256: value.sha256 } : {} }
571	        break
572	      }
573	      case 'tree':
574	        // Only a comparator naming `tree` reaches here, and such a case is
575	        // executed with the scope its check declares.
576	        expectation = { ...expectation, treeSha256: await hashWorkspaceTree(capture.scope as string, normalizers) }
577	        break
578	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
579	      default:
580	        return assertNever(channel)
581	    }
582	  }
583	  return expectation
584	}

586	/** One rendered cluster with the check facts its line names. */
587	interface RenderedCluster extends DirectiveCluster {
588	  readonly outcome: string
589	  readonly total: number
590	  readonly weightTotal: number
591	  readonly exitClass: CaseExitClass
592	}

594	/** Group one cased check's failed cases by the channels that disagreed and how the candidate ended. */
595	function clustersOf(check: StandardCheck, result: CheckResult): RenderedCluster[] {
596	  const cases = result.cases
597	  /* v8 ignore next -- only a cased result reaches here, and a cased result carries its tally */
598	  if (cases === undefined) return []
599	  const clusters = new Map<string, RenderedCluster>()
600	  for (const failed of cases.failed) {
601	    const key = `${failed.exitClass}|${failed.channels.join(',')}`
602	    const existing = clusters.get(key)
603	    clusters.set(key, {
604	      checkId: result.checkId,
605	      channels: failed.channels,
606	      count: (existing?.count ?? 0) + 1,
607	      weight: (existing?.weight ?? 0) + failed.weight,
608	      outcome: check.outcome,
609	      total: cases.total,
610	      weightTotal: cases.weightTotal,
611	      exitClass: failed.exitClass,
612	    })
613	  }
614	  return [...clusters.values()]
615	}

617	/**
618	 * One directive per failed run. A cased check contributes one line per failure
619	 * cluster, naming its authored outcome, the cluster's count and weight, the
620	 * channels that disagreed, and how the candidate ended — never a case body, an
621	 * expected digest, or a byte of captured output. A check without cases
622	 * contributes its recorded evidence line.
623	 * @param failures - the run's failing results, in check order.
624	 * @param checks - the standard's active checks, supplying each outcome text.
625	 * @param maxChars - bound of the rendered detail.
626	 * @returns the directive, carrying `clusters` when a cased check failed.
627	 */
628	function describeFailures(
629	  failures: readonly CheckResult[],
630	  checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
631	  maxChars: number,
632	): DirectiveRequest {
633	  const lines: string[] = []
634	  const clusters: DirectiveCluster[] = []
635	  for (const failure of failures) {
636	    const check = checks.find(candidate => candidate.id === failure.checkId)
637	    if (check === undefined || failure.cases === undefined) {
638	      lines.push(failure.evidence)
639	      continue
640	    }
641	    for (const cluster of clustersOf(check, failure)) {
642	      clusters.push({ checkId: cluster.checkId, channels: cluster.channels, count: cluster.count, weight: cluster.weight })
643	      lines.push(`${cluster.outcome}: ${cluster.count} of ${cluster.total} cases failed (weight ${cluster.weight} of ${cluster.weightTotal}); mismatching channels: ${cluster.channels.join(', ')}; ${EXIT_PHRASE[cluster.exitClass]}`)
644	    }
645	  }
646	  return {
647	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
648	    detail: bound(lines.map((line, index) => `${index + 1}. ${line}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
649	    ...clusters.length === 0 ? {} : { clusters },
650	  }
651	}

675	  if (seed === undefined && topP === undefined) return undefined

682	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
683	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
684	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
685	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
686	  ))
687	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
688	  const total: TokenUsage = {
689	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
690	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
691	  }
692	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
693	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
694	      const value = step[key]
695	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
696	    })
697	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
698	  }
699	  return total
700	}

1036	  private async executeCases(

1038	    cases: readonly CheckCase[],
1039	    command: string,
1040	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
1041	  ): Promise<CasedCheckRun> {

1044	    let weightPassed = 0

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the environment runner: the run request and the run report,
3	 * free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel, EnvironmentRunStamp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
9	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
10	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
11	import type { CheckResult, VerificationCertificate } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
12	
13	/** One request to run a registered environment as one fresh session. */
14	export interface EnvironmentRunRequest {
15	  /** Registered environment to run. */
16	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
17	  /** Existing absolute directory the session is rooted at; the task fixture is overlaid onto it. */
18	  readonly workspace: string
19	  /** Model route for this run; absent uses the composition's default model selection. */
20	  readonly model?: EnvironmentRunModel
21	  /** Zero-based repetition of this environment inside its batch; absent means `0`. */
22	  readonly repetition?: number
23	  /** Batch or sampling group the run belongs to, absent for a single run. */
24	  readonly group?: string
25	  /** District the run belongs to, written into the stamp so exports can withhold it; absent for a run outside every district. */
26	  readonly district?: string
27	  /**
28	   * Checkpoint or policy the implementer route serves, as the deployment names
29	   * it, written into the stamp verbatim; absent for a route the deployment did
30	   * not version.
31	   */
32	  readonly policyVersion?: string
33	  /**
34	   * Sampling seed every request of the run asks for, a safe non-negative
35	   * integer written into the stamp; absent leaves the composition's own
36	   * sampling in place.
37	   */
38	  readonly seed?: number
39	  /** Aborts the implementer's turns and the check commands when it fires. */
40	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
41	}
42	
43	/**
44	 * One attempt: the implementer's turn followed by one run of the current
45	 * standard. The attempt's verdict is durable rather than reported: it is the
46	 * `verdict` of the `verification/run` this attempt recorded.
47	 */
48	export interface EnvironmentRunAttempt {
49	  /** One-based attempt number. */
50	  readonly attempt: number
51	  /** One result per active check, in the standard's check order; a tampered attempt executed none of them. */
52	  readonly results: readonly CheckResult[]
53	  /**
54	   * SHA-256 digest of the workspace as the validation began, after the fixture
55	   * was restored over it; a tampered attempt digests the workspace it refused
56	   * to measure, without restoring anything.
57	   */
58	  readonly treeHash: string
59	}
60	
61	/** Outcome of one environment run, returned after the session is flushed. */
62	export interface EnvironmentRunReport {
63	  /** Environment that was run. */
64	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
65	  /** Session the run created; its log is the durable record. */
66	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
67	  /** The `environment/run` stamp the session log carries, exactly as appended. */
68	  readonly stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp
69	  /** Every attempt in order; the last one decided `certified`. */
70	  readonly attempts: readonly EnvironmentRunAttempt[]
71	  /** Whether a run of the standard passed completely and the goal completed. */
72	  readonly certified: boolean
73	  /** Certificate of the passing run, present exactly when `certified` is `true`. */
74	  readonly certificate?: VerificationCertificate
75	  /** Model usage summed over every assistant message of the session, absent when the model produced none. */
76	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage
77	}
