1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Environment runner: one registered environment as one fresh, validated session. The runner stamps the session with the environment it runs, creates the goal, authors the completion standard from the environment's checks, drives the implementer turn by turn, executes the checks through the shell executor after each turn, records the run, and completes the goal only under a certificate. The [environment-runner Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: environments
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
12	- id: agent-default-model
13	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
14	  config:
15	    provider: deepseek-official
16	    model: deepseek-v4-flash
17	- id: environment-runner
18	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
19	  config:
20	    isolation: none
21	    maxAttempts: 2
22	    maxGoalRounds: 8
23	    checkTimeoutMs: 120000
24	    evidenceMaxChars: 2000
25	    maxFailedCases: 20
26	    topP: 0.95
27	```
28	
29	| Field | Meaning |
30	|---|---|
31	| `isolation` (required) | `none`, `process`, or `host`: the isolation the deployment can defend for its check runs. A local composition that shares the filesystem between implementer and validator is `none`; a run whose checks and fixtures live on another account or host is `host`. Written into every certificate and stamp; nothing in-process can verify it. |
32	| `maxAttempts` (default `1`) | Implementer turns before the run is reported uncertified; each turn is followed by one validation. |
33	| `maxGoalRounds` (optional) | Round cap handed to goal creation; absent applies the goal service default. |
34	| `checkTimeoutMs` (optional) | Timeout override for each check command and each case, capped by the executor; absent applies the executor default. |
35	| `evidenceMaxChars` (default `2000`) | Bound of each evidence string and of the directive detail. It must not exceed the verification service's `maxTextChars`, or `recordRun` rejects the result loudly. |
36	| `maxFailedCases` (default `20`) | Failed cases one check result names. The rest are still counted and weighed in the tally; only their per-case entries are dropped, which is what keeps a run of hundreds of cases out of the log. |
37	| `topP` (optional) | Nucleus-sampling mass between 0 and 1 every request of every run asks for. It is a deployment choice rather than a per-run one: a suite compares cells only while every cell samples the same way. Absent leaves the composition's own sampling in place. |
38	
39	The service requires `environments`, `agents`, `agentDefaultModel`, `goals`, `completionStandards`, `shell`, and `sessions`. It also uses [`ctx.readBarrier`](../../verification/read-barrier/README.md) when the composition provides it; without it the run reserves nothing and the checks execute their instructions inline, which is what an `isolation: none` claim already says.
40	
41	## Service contract
42	
43	`ctx.environmentRuns.run({ environment, workspace, model?, repetition?, group?, district?, policyVersion?, seed?, signal? })` reads the definition from the registry, overlays `task.fixture` (an existing absolute directory) onto `workspace` and hashes its files, and creates a fresh agent with `meta.cwd = workspace`, the requested `model` route or the composition's default selection, and the model-selection setup the headless bundle uses. Before anything else enters the log it appends the `environment/run` stamp: environment id and kind, `heldOut`, the content hashes of prompt, fixture, and checks, `repetition` (default `0`), `group`, and `district`, the `policyVersion` and `seed` the run asked for, the model route, and the configured isolation. It then creates the goal from the task prompt, disarms it so a composed goal-round driver never continues it, and authors the standard from the environment's checks verbatim.
44	
45	With a barrier composed, the run reserves `<barrier root>/runs/<sessionId>/` before the stamp, copies a held-out environment's fixture to `fixture/` and any [declared reference](#the-staged-reference) to `reference/` there, and rewrites each attempt's check command to source a script the reservation holds. The reservation is stocked before the implementer's first turn and again at each attempt with `standard.json` and one `checks/<checkId>/` directory per active check, holding its `run` script and, for a check that carries cases, the `cases.jsonl` those cases live in — so the implementer sees a command line naming a file whose content the barrier denies it. A check id that is not a single path segment, and a reservation path the check command line cannot carry unquoted, both fail the run with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT`.
46	
47	Each attempt sends the prompt as a user turn, waits for whole-agent idle, [digests the check-owned set](#tamper-on-check-owned-paths), overlays `task.fixture` onto the workspace again so implementer edits to validator-owned files never reach the checks, digests the workspace files, and executes every active check of the current standard through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace`. A check without cases runs once: exit code `0` without timeout or abort is `pass`, anything else `fail`; evidence is the exit fact followed by the bounded tails of stdout and stderr. A check with cases runs [once per case](#weighted-cases-and-the-reservation). `recordRun` records the run under `{ executor: 'runner', treeHash }` — one durable `verification/run` event per attempt, passing or failing, carrying `parity` when any check had cases — and commits a certificate or returns the failing subset. Certified: the goal is completed, which the verification guard admits. Not certified: one [directive](#the-clustered-directive) is recorded, and while attempts remain the next turn carries it in a `<validation_failed>` block.
48	
49	## Sampling and what a replay reproduces
50	
51	The request's `seed` and the deployment's `topP` are pinned on the agent's model selection, so every request the cell makes carries the same sampling and each is reconstructable from the session's `request/header` events. `seed` must be a safe non-negative integer; anything else fails the run with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_SEED` before an agent exists. The stamp carries `seed` because it is what distinguishes two cells of one plan; `topP` is constant across the deployment and stays in the request header alone.
52	
53	A seed records what the run **asked for**, never what the provider did. An adapter whose wire has no `seed` field drops it, a provider that accepts one may still ignore it, and no provider promises identical tokens across model or infrastructure versions. What a replay reproduces is the session log — the prompt, the tools, the header, and the transcript — not a fresh sample from the model.
54	
55	`policyVersion` is free-form text naming the checkpoint or policy the route served; the runner writes it into the stamp verbatim and never resolves it, so a fold keying measured difficulty by policy version compares the strings its logs carry.
56	
57	## Weighted cases and the reservation
58	
59	For a check whose environment supplied [case bodies](../environments/README.md#weighted-cases), the runner runs the candidate once per case in the workspace, in authored order. Each case empties the check's `treeScope` when it declares one, stages the case's `files`, appends the case's `argv` words to the check's command line, and feeds its `stdin`. Every configured channel is then normalized and digested: `exit` against `expected.exitCode`, `stdout` and `stderr` against their digests, and `tree` against the digest of every regular file under `treeScope` as the case left it. A truncated stream fails its channel, because the executor dropped bytes the digest covers. A case passes only when every configured channel matched.
60	
61	The result carries `cases: { passed, total, weightPassed, weightTotal, failed }`; its status follows the cases, so one failing case fails the check. `failed` names up to `maxFailedCases` entries, each with the mismatching channels and the exit class (`zero`, `nonzero`, `signal`, or `timeout`). Evidence is the tally line followed by each named failure with its own exit fact and captured output — the raw bytes stay in the session log, which the read barrier denies an implementer.
62	
63	## The clustered directive
64	
65	A failed run issues one directive. `rootCause` names the count of failing checks. `detail` is one numbered line per entry: a cased check contributes one line per failure cluster — its failed cases grouped by the channels that disagreed and by exit class — naming the check's validator-authored `outcome`, the cluster's count and weight against the check's totals, the channels, and how the candidate ended; a check without cases contributes its recorded evidence line. The event also carries `clusters: [{ checkId, channels, count, weight }]` for the observatory, and `detail` stays bounded by `evidenceMaxChars`.
66	
67	A cluster line names no case id, no expected digest, and no byte of captured output: what a hidden case expects is the case, so a wall that holds on the filesystem and leaks through the directive holds nothing. A caseless check keeps forwarding its evidence line, which is the older rendering an environment migrates away from by giving its checks cases.
68	
69	The report carries the environment id, the session id, the stamp exactly as appended, one entry per attempt with its check results and workspace digest, `certified`, the certificate when one run passed, and the model usage summed over the session's assistant messages. The session is flushed and the agent handle disposed on every path, including a thrown error.
70	
71	`EnvironmentRunError` codes: `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT`, `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_SEED`, `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE`, and `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE` reject before any agent exists; `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT`, `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED`, and `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST` name a check the reservation cannot carry, an implementer that replaced the goal, or a standard that is no longer current, after the session was flushed; `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_NO_REFERENCE` and `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_NO_RESERVATION` refuse a reference staging the environment or the composition cannot support. `resolveConfig(config)` is the exported defaulting step.
72	
73	Call `run()` only over a settled composition: the runner creates agents through the registry factory the agent loop registers. The durable record is the session log; the trajectory exporter folds it into a `dsh-trajectory/1` line whose `environment` field is the stamp and withholds held-out sessions by it.
74	
75	## The staged reference
76	
77	An environment that declares [`task.reference`](../environments/README.md#the-reference-directory) hides one directory of its fixture from the implementer and hands it to the validator. Every overlay of the fixture — the first one and the one before each validation — deletes that directory from the workspace afterwards, so the implementer's tree never holds it; the reservation receives a copy at `reference/`, where the barrier denies an implementer every read. The reference sits inside the reservation, so the [check-owned digest](#tamper-on-check-owned-paths) already covers it: rewriting the reference under the validator voids the attempt exactly as rewriting a check script does.
78	
79	`ctx.environmentRuns.stageReference(agent, environmentId)` mints one agent's reservation and stocks it with that environment's reference, for a validator deriving the standard before any implementer runs. It resolves the reference to the same `reference/run` entry the runner's own reservation carries, so [the instrument](../../verification/tool-standard-author/README.md) finds it at one path whichever session holds it. An unknown environment, one that declares no reference, and a composition with no read barrier are refused with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT`, `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_NO_REFERENCE`, and `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_NO_RESERVATION`.
80	
81	`captureCase(shell, execution)` and `caseExpectation(capture, comparator)` are exported for the same reason: the runner measures a candidate with them and the instrument records a reference with them, so what a case means is one procedure rather than two that can drift. `captureCase` empties the `treeScope`, stages the case's files, appends its `argv`, and feeds its `stdin`; `caseExpectation` digests the channels a comparator names and leaves out a channel the run could put no value on — a signalled exit, a stream the executor truncated.
82	
83	## Tamper on check-owned paths
84	
85	The check-owned set is the barrier's reserved directory, when one was minted, plus every path the environment declares in [`task.immutable`](../environments/README.md#the-immutable-set): a declared file digests its bytes, a declared directory its whole tree, and a declared path that is gone digests as absent, so a deletion counts as much as a rewrite. The runner digests the whole set once before the implementer's first turn and again at the start of every attempt, before the fixture is restored — the overlay would otherwise put back exactly what the comparison is looking for.
86	
87	A digest that differs from the one the validator left ends the run: no check is executed, every result of that attempt records that it was not, `recordRun` receives `tampered: true` and writes `verdict: 'tampered'`, no certificate can follow it, the goal stays out of `complete`, one directive states the tamper, and the implementer receives it as its last validation follow-up. The trajectory exporter reads the recorded verdict and scores the session `0` on its `tamper` basis. After every validation the runner re-digests the set it just rewrote, so its own `standard.json` and check scripts are the baseline the next attempt is measured against.
88	
89	## Model Experience
90	
91	### Task prompt and validation follow-up
92	
93	#### What the model sees
94	
95	The environment's `task.prompt` arrives as the first user message of a fresh session with the composition's ordinary system prompt and tools; the checks never appear. After a failed validation, while attempts remain, the next user message is the block below, where `<rootCause>` reads `N of the standard's checks failed` and `<detail>` numbers one line per failure cluster of a cased check — its authored outcome, the cluster's count and weight, the channels that disagreed, and how the candidate ended — and one evidence line (exit fact, stdout and stderr tails) per failing check without cases, bounded by `evidenceMaxChars`. A tampered attempt sends the same block carrying the fixed tamper directive below and then ends the run; that text names neither a path nor a check, because a digest comparison knows that the check-owned set changed and nothing more.
96	
97	##### Validation follow-up
98	
99	```markdown
100	<validation_failed>
101	<rootCause>
102	<detail>
103	Continue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.
104	</validation_failed>
105	```
106	
107	##### Tamper follow-up
108	
109	```markdown
110	<validation_failed>
111	the files this task is measured with were modified during the attempt
112	Those files belong to the validator: the task is to make them pass, never to change them. This run is void and no certificate can follow it.
113	Continue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.
114	</validation_failed>
115	```
116	
117	#### Token effect
118	
119	One user message per attempt: the prompt, then one follow-up block per failed validation whose size is bounded by `evidenceMaxChars`. The tamper follow-up is fixed text. Nothing is added to the system prompt or to tool schemas.
120	
121	#### KV Cache effect
122	
123	Append-only: each follow-up extends the same session after its reusable prefix, so the conversation prefix stays cacheable across attempts.
124	
125	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
126	
127	- **The barrier covers filesystem reads only** — an implementer preset that composes a log-reading tool, or a bash check-running executor, still reaches the standard through a seam the barrier does not fence; a certificate from this runner is as strong as the configured `isolation` claim, which nothing here verifies.
128	- **A reserved check runs by being sourced** — the command line is `. <script>`, which a POSIX shell executor runs exactly as it would the inline instruction; a composed PowerShell executor cannot source an extensionless file, so such a deployment runs without a barrier.
129	- **The fixture overlay is the only restoration** — each validation restores validator-owned fixture files, but files the implementer added outside the fixture stay in the workspace and reach the checks.
130	- **Tamper detection is a digest comparison** — it reports that the check-owned set changed, never who changed it or how, so a legitimate build step that rewrites a file inside the immutable set voids its run; environment authors declare the set narrowly, and a false verdict costs one run rather than a wrong certificate.
131	- **Command checks only** — a check whose `run` is a procedure fails as a non-zero exit with the evidence saying so; judges belong to the oversight seam.
132	- **Sequential checks and cases, one repetition per call** — checks run one after another in the workspace and a cased check runs its cases in authored order, so a large case set costs one executor start per case; group sampling repeats `run()` with `repetition` and `group` set by the caller.
133	- **A case's `argv` rides the check's command line** — the words are appended verbatim and must need no shell quoting, which authoring enforces, because the composed shell's dialect is not known where the standard is authored. A case that needs an argument holding spaces stages it as a file instead.
134	- **A caseless check still forwards its output** — the clustered directive closes the wall for cased checks; a check that carries no cases keeps sending its bounded stdout and stderr tails to the implementer.
135	- **Fixture overlay does not clear the workspace** — same-named files are overwritten; the runner refuses a workspace that is not a directory but does not require it to be empty.

179	/**
180	 * A provider's detached contribution to one continuable child's creation. This
181	 * is DATA, never a capability: it carries no Agent, `AgentHandle`, prompt
182	 * delivery, result, disposal, or resume operation, because the continuation
183	 * manager owns the child's whole lifecycle after preparation.
184	 */
185	export interface ContinuableCreateSpec {
186	  /**
187	   * Completed-turn prefix of the parent's log to seed the child session with,
188	   * or absent for a fresh child. Same durable contract as
189	   * `CreateAgentOptions.seed`: contiguous from seq 0, lossless JSON, balanced.
190	   */

194	/**
195	 * Why a subagent run ended. Merge-extensible (a backend may add variants);
196	 * consumers branch on the known cases and fall through `default`. The known
197	 * cases mirror the harness turn-end vocabulary so the tool layer can map a
198	 * non-`completed` result to an `isError` tool result.
199	 */
200	export interface SubagentStopReasonMap {
201	  /** The child finished its turn normally. */
202	  completed: 'completed'
203	  /** Cancelled through the request signal or disposal. */
204	  aborted: 'aborted'
205	  /** Model or transport failure. */
206	  error: 'error'
207	  /** The child hit its token ceiling before finishing. */
208	  'max-tokens': 'max-tokens'

213	/** The union over {@link SubagentStopReasonMap} — widens automatically as backends merge in variants. */
214	export type SubagentStopReason = SubagentStopReasonMap[keyof SubagentStopReasonMap]

216	/**
217	 * The terminal outcome of a subagent run, resolved by {@link SubagentRun.result}.
218	 */

220	  /**

222	   * assistant message. Empty-content messages, including usage-only messages,
223	   * are skipped. Without a non-empty message, the output is its accumulated

240	/**

242	 * work, and infrastructure faults after that boundary belong to {@link result}.

244	 * remaining work and reach quiescence. A run is one disposable foreground
245	 * delegation with one result; continuable conversations have no run — the
246	 * continuation manager holds their `AgentHandle` directly and orders every
247	 * turn through the child's own inbox.

259	   * implication beyond the run's ordinary {@link dispose} contract.
260	   */

262	  /**

264	   * settles. Does NOT reject on a child-level failure — a model/transport

266	   * `isError` tool result. Rejects on an infrastructure fault the seam cannot
267	   * represent as a stop reason.
268	   */

270	  /**
271	   * Cancel remaining work, reach child quiescence, and release resources.
272	   * Idempotent.
273	   */

275	}

277	/**

279	 * same-process implementations; callers treat descriptors and returned values

281	 * for distinct children. Providers isolate operation-local mutable state; a
282	 * shared capacity controller may delay an operation but must not couple its
283	 * settlement or cleanup to a sibling.

298	   * The service has already validated that every requested start-time
299	   * capability is supported and resolved `request.descriptor`, so a
300	   * session-backed implementation appends that descriptor inside the child's

311	   * only whether the child session is seeded with parent history. Method
312	   * presence IS the capability: the service rejects continuable starts on
313	   * providers without it, while a provider that has it may still serve
314	   * ordinary one-shot delegations.
315	   *

317	   * continuation manager owns identity reservation, composition, Agent
318	   * creation, prompt delivery, cold resume, ownership, and disposal, so a
319	   * provider never sees the child's Agent, handle, turns, or teardown.
320	   * Distinct preparations may overlap; each follows its own signal and returns
321	   * data belonging only to `request.sessionId`.
322	   */

227	   * @param parent - the exact live direct parent authorizing this delivery.
228	   * @param childId - durable child session id.
229	   * @param content - user-role content to deliver.
230	   * @param options - the message source fields and caller cancellation, which stops the
231	   *   operation only before inbox acceptance.
232	   * @returns the accepted message's inbox id.
233	   * @throws when continuation services are unavailable, parent authority is
234	   *   rejected, or the message was not admitted.
235	   */
236	  async followup(
237	    parent: Agent,
238	    childId: SessionId,
239	    content: ContentBlock[],
240	    options: SubagentFollowupOptions,
241	  ): Promise<MessageId> {
242	    return this.requireContinuations().followup(parent, childId, content, options)
243	  }
244	
245	  /**
246	   * Interrupt one live continuable child's current turn under a human parent
247	   * address or an exact live ancestor Agent. Fire-and-return: the cancel
248	   * signal is issued before this returns, but the target may keep running
249	   * until it observes the signal. Unclaimed pending inbox work, the Activation,
250	   * and published descendants are preserved; claimed work is not requeued.
251	   * Once the interrupted driver is idle, a waking send resumes the parked FIFO
252	   * queue. An absent target — including a one-shot or unknown id —
253	   * is an accepted no-op, as is a manager-less composition, which cannot own a
254	   * live Activation.
255	   * @param targetSessionId - the durable child session id to interrupt.
256	   * @param authority - the human parent address or exact live ancestor Agent.
257	   * @throws {SubagentError} `UNAUTHORIZED` when the authority does not own the
258	   *   live target.
259	   */
260	  interrupt(targetSessionId: SessionId, authority: SubagentInterruptAuthority): void {
261	    this.continuations?.interrupt(targetSessionId, authority)
262	  }
263	
264	  /**
265	   * Deliver selected content from one live continuable child to its durable
266	   * direct parent. The child is the authority credential; callers cannot name a
267	   * recipient. Reporting does not conclude the child's turn or Activation.
268	   * @param child - exact live reporting child.
269	   * @param content - selected model-facing content.
270	   * @param options - parent scheduling and pre-acceptance cancellation.
271	   * @returns the stable identity of the parent-accepted message.
272	   * @throws when continuation services are unavailable, sender authorization
273	   *   fails, or the direct parent is not live.
274	   */
275	  async reportFrom(
276	    child: Agent,
277	    content: ContentBlock[],
278	    options: SubagentReportOptions,
279	  ): Promise<MessageId> {
280	    return this.requireContinuations().reportFrom(child, content, options)
281	  }
282	
283	  /**
284	   * Compose one deployment capability into every continuable child's
285	   * unpublished creation context on fresh creation and cold resume. Grants wait
286	   * for the next Activation; removing the contribution revokes every resident
287	   * installation immediately.
288	   * @param contribution - synchronous child-scope installer.
289	   * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer.
290	   */
291	  registerContinuableSetup(contribution: ContinuableSetupContribution): () => void {
292	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
293	    return this.ctx.effect(
294	      () => this.setupRegistry.register(contribution),
295	      'subagents.registerContinuableSetup()',
296	    )
297	  }
298	
299	  /**
300	   * Close continuable admission below exact live parent Agents, stop only their
301	   * visible descendant Activations synchronously, then await admitted scoped
302	   * materializations and release those forests child-first. The scoped cutoff
303	   * lasts until each exact parent leaves the registry; unrelated parent trees
304	   * remain live.
305	   * @param parents - exact host-owned parent Agents entering teardown.
306	   * @returns once every retained descendant Activation released its `AgentHandle`.
307	   * @throws an aggregate error after all branches settle when any failed.
308	   */
309	  async drainContinuableDescendants(parents: readonly Agent[]): Promise<void> {
310	    const manager = this.continuations
311	    // Absent continuation services means nothing was ever materialized.
312	    if (manager === undefined) return
313	    await manager.drainDescendants(parents)
314	  }
315	
316	  /**
317	   * Enumerate the parent's direct session-backed subagents without loading or
318	   * resuming an Agent and without any query service: the listing merges the live
319	   * session store with optional session persistence (live-preferred) and
320	   * serves each child's durable mode/label from the registered `subagent`
321	   * projection unit down a three-rung ladder — the registry's watermark
322	   * snapshot for a live child; for a cold one, a durable projection-cache
323	   * row when the optional cache serves an own-suffix identity (its `seq`
324	   * gate proves the value postdates the fork seed, where a child's own
325	   * descriptor is immutable once appended), else one persistence inspection
326	   * folded through the registry. The
327	   * projection fold is the single classification authority; per-child
328	   * diagnostics relay a fold that served no identity or a failed inspection,
329	   * never a list-time descriptor parse. Absent persistence, enumeration is
330	   * live-only (a cold child cannot be resumed then either, so its absence is
331	   * capability absence, not an error). This service consults no Agent
332	   * registrations, Activations, or providers.
333	   *
334	   * Every persistence read receives `signal`, and the listing rechecks
335	   * cancellation around each of those awaits. Read rejections that settle
336	   * after an abort become a stable `SubagentError` with code `CANCELLED`.
337	   * @param parentSessionId - parent session whose direct children are listed.
338	   * @param signal - caller-owned cancellation forwarded to persistence reads
339	   *   and observed around every read await.
340	   * @returns children and per-child diagnostics ordered by `createdAt`, then id.
341	   * @throws {@link SubagentError} when the projection registry or the session
342	   *   store is not mounted, or the caller cancels the listing.
343	   */
344	  listChildren(parentSessionId: SessionId, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SubagentListEntry[]> {
345	    return listSubagentChildren(this.ctx, parentSessionId, signal)
346	  }
347	
348	  /**
349	   * Enumerate the root's complete session-backed subagent tree in stable
350	   * pre-order from one live-preferred corpus, without loading or resuming an
351	   * Agent. Ordinary sessions and one-shot children remain traversal nodes so
352	   * continuable descendants below them are discovered; each returned entry
353	   * adds its durable `parentId` and root-relative `depth`. Identity resolution,
354	   * diagnostics, optional persistence, and cancellation follow the same
355	   * projection-backed contract as {@link listChildren}.
356	   * @param rootSessionId - session whose complete descendant tree is listed.
357	   * @param signal - caller-owned cancellation forwarded to persistence reads
358	   *   and observed around every read await.
359	   * @returns children and per-candidate diagnostics with tree position, in
360	   *   stable pre-order.
361	   * @throws {@link SubagentError} under the same conditions as {@link listChildren}.
362	   */
363	  listDescendants(rootSessionId: SessionId, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SubagentDescendantListEntry[]> {
364	    return listSubagentDescendants(this.ctx, rootSessionId, signal)
365	  }
366	
367	  /**
368	   * Register a provider under its name. Registration is effect-scoped and HMR
369	   * safe; removing a provider blocks new starts but does not revoke runs that
370	   * were already returned to their holders.
371	   * @param provider - the trusted provider implementation.
372	   * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer.
373	   */
374	  registerProvider(provider: SubagentProvider): () => void {
375	    const name = provider.name
376	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
377	    return this.ctx.effect(function* (this: SubagentRuntime) {
378	      if (this.providers.has(name)) {
379	        throw new SubagentError(`a subagent provider named "${name}" is already registered`, 'DUPLICATE_PROVIDER')
380	      }
381	      this.providers.set(name, provider)
382	      yield () => {
383	        this.providers.delete(name)
384	        this.emitLifecycle('subagent/provider-removed', name)
385	      }
386	      // A throwing added-listener unwinds the yielded rollback, matching the
387	      // repository's fail-loud registration semantics.
388	      this.ctx.emit('subagent/provider-added', provider)
389	    }.bind(this), 'subagents.registerProvider()')
390	  }
391	
392	  /**
393	   * Look up a provider by name.
394	   * @param name - the provider name.
395	   * @returns the provider, or undefined when absent.
396	   */
397	  getProvider(name: string): SubagentProvider | undefined {
398	    return this.providers.get(name)
399	  }
400	
401	  /**
402	   * List registered provider names in insertion order.
403	   * @returns the registered names.
404	   */
405	  list(): string[] {
406	    return [...this.providers.keys()]
407	  }
408	
409	  /**
410	   * Establish a published child on the named provider. Capability and semantic
411	   * checks run before delegation. Provider ownership lasts until its promise
412	   * fulfills; a rejection therefore has no run for the caller to dispose and
413	   * emits no run lifecycle events. Post-publication turn and infrastructure
414	   * failures settle through the returned run.
415	   * @param name - the provider to use.
416	   * @param request - child label, prompt, parent, signal, and optional capabilities.
417	   * @returns the published holder-owned run.
418	   */
419	  async start(name: string, request: SubagentStartRequest): Promise<SubagentRun> {
420	    const provider = this.expectProvider(name)
421	    this.assertCapabilities(provider, request)
422	    assertSubagentMaxDepth(request.maxDepth)
423	    if (request.outputSchema !== undefined) assertObjectJsonSchema(request.outputSchema)
424	    const descriptor = snapshotSubagentDescriptor({
425	      mode: 'one-shot',
426	      provider: name,
427	      ...request.label !== undefined ? { label: request.label } : {},
428	    })
429	    const resolved: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest = { ...request, descriptor }
430	    return observeRun(this.emitLifecycle, name, request.parent, await provider.start(resolved))
431	  }
432	
433	  /**
434	   * Resolve one provider's detached continuable-creation contribution. Method
435	   * presence on the provider IS the capability, so a provider without it is
436	   * rejected before the manager reserves any child resources.
437	   */
438	  private async prepareContinuable(
439	    name: string,
440	    request: ContinuableCreateRequest,
441	  ): Promise<ContinuableCreateSpec> {
442	    const provider = this.expectProvider(name)
443	    if (provider.prepareContinuable === undefined) {
444	      throw new SubagentError(
445	        `subagent provider "${provider.name}" does not support continuable children `
446	        + '(no prepareContinuable capability)',
447	        'UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY',
448	      )
449	    }
450	    return provider.prepareContinuable(request)
451	  }
452	
453	  /** Look up a provider for dispatch or fail loud. */
454	  private expectProvider(name: string): SubagentProvider {
455	    const provider = this.providers.get(name)
456	    if (provider === undefined) {
457	      throw new SubagentError(`no subagent provider registered for "${name}"`, 'NO_PROVIDER')
458	    }
459	    return provider
460	  }
461	
462	  /** Resolve the optional continuable-subagent manager or fail loud. */
463	  private requireContinuations(): SubagentContinuationManager {
464	    if (this.continuations === undefined) {
465	      throw new SubagentError(
466	        'continuable subagents require the agents service',
467	        'CONTINUATION_UNAVAILABLE',
468	      )
469	    }
470	    return this.continuations
471	  }
472	
473	  /**
474	   * Build the lifecycle observer for one continuable Activation's residency
475	   * epoch, so the manager publishes its edges without owning event dispatch.
476	   */
477	  private observeActivation(
478	    provider: string,
479	    childId: SessionId,
480	    parent: Agent,
481	  ): ActivationObserver {
482	    return createActivationObserver(this.emitLifecycle, provider, childId, parent)
483	  }
484	
485	  /** Reject the first requested capability that the provider lacks. */
486	  private assertCapabilities(provider: SubagentProvider, request: SubagentStartRequest): void {
487	    const needs: { when: boolean; cap: keyof SubagentCapabilities }[] = [
488	      { when: request.outputSchema !== undefined, cap: 'outputSchema' },
489	      { when: request.maxDepth !== undefined, cap: 'depthLimit' },
490	      { when: request.toolFilter !== undefined, cap: 'toolFilter' },
491	      { when: request.persona !== undefined, cap: 'persona' },
492	    ]
493	    for (const { when, cap } of needs) {
494	      if (when && !provider.capabilities[cap]) {
495	        throw new SubagentError(
496	          `subagent provider "${provider.name}" does not support the "${cap}" capability`,
497	          'UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY',
498	        )
499	      }
500	    }
501	  }
502	}
503	
504	export default SubagentRuntime

1	/**
2	 * What every OUT-OF-PROCESS subagent provider does about the read barrier. Such
3	 * a child launches a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness
4	 * policy, so no fence this process installs reaches its reads: the only denial
5	 * available to it is not starting.
6	 *
7	 * In-process drivers need none of this. A child that joins its parent's standing
8	 * composition through `composeFrom()` inherits the same census, the same scope
9	 * layer, and the same role, so the parent's own executors already deny it.
10	 *
11	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent/read-barrier
12	 */
13	
14	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
16	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
17	import { SubagentError } from './error.ts'
18	
19	/** Code carried by the refusal, so a caller routes it without parsing the message. */
20	export const SUBAGENT_READ_BARRIER_REFUSED = 'READ_BARRIER_REFUSED'
21	
22	/**
23	 * Record that this provider enforces the read barrier by refusing to start.
24	 * Loader siblings mount concurrently, so the registration waits for the barrier
25	 * and unwinds with it; a composition with no barrier registers nothing.
26	 * @param ctx - the provider's plugin context.
27	 */
28	export function enforceOutOfProcessRefusal(ctx: Context): void {
29	  ctx.inject(['readBarrier'], (scope: Context) => { scope.readBarrier.enforceByRefusal('subagent') })
30	}
31	
32	/**
33	 * Refuse one out-of-process child the read barrier will not allow, in the
34	 * operation that would launch it.
35	 * @param ctx - the provider's plugin context; the barrier is optional.
36	 * @param parent - the delegating parent agent, whose session holds the role.
37	 * @throws {@link SubagentError} with {@link SUBAGENT_READ_BARRIER_REFUSED} when
38	 *   the barrier refuses this session's out-of-process children.
39	 */
40	export function assertOutOfProcessAllowed(ctx: Context, parent: Agent): void {
41	  const refusal = ctx.get('readBarrier')?.startRefusal('subagent', parent.session)
42	  if (refusal !== undefined) throw new SubagentError(refusal, SUBAGENT_READ_BARRIER_REFUSED)
43	}
44

1	/**
2	 * Provider-side vocabulary for OUT-OF-PROCESS subagent backends — the pieces
3	 * that enforce this seam's own contracts around a child in another process:
4	 * the no-capabilities advertisement, timing-bound validation, child
5	 * working-directory resolution (config override, else the delegating parent
6	 * session's workspace), the never-reject result settlement, and the standard
7	 * run-handle publication. Backends compose these with their own wire drivers;
8	 * the process machinery itself (spawn, env scrub, tree-scoped teardown)
9	 * belongs to the `dsh-subprocess` seam.
10	 *
11	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent/out-of-process
12	 */
13	
14	import { accessSync, constants, statSync } from 'node:fs'
15	import { isAbsolute, resolve } from 'node:path'
16	import type { ContentBlock } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
17	import type { SubagentCapabilities, SubagentResult, SubagentRun, SubagentStopReason } from './types.ts'
18	
19	/**
20	 * The capability advertisement of an out-of-process backend: NONE. A child in
21	 * another process cannot honor parent-enforced start features
22	 * (`outputSchema`/`maxDepth`/`toolFilter`/`persona`), so the service rejects a
23	 * request needing any of them before `start` runs — never accepted-then-ignored.
24	 */
25	export const NO_START_CAPABILITIES: SubagentCapabilities = Object.freeze({
26	  outputSchema: false,
27	  depthLimit: false,
28	  toolFilter: false,
29	  persona: false,
30	})
31	
32	/**
33	 * Assert a configured timing bound is a positive finite number (it bounds a
34	 * teardown or shutdown wait; zero, negative, or NaN would skip or wedge it).
35	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix (e.g. `subagent-acp`).
36	 * @param name - the config field name, for the diagnostic.
37	 * @param value - the configured value.
38	 */
39	export function assertPositiveFinite(prefix: string, name: string, value: number): void {
40	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) {
41	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: ${name} must be a positive finite number`)
42	  }
43	}
44	
45	/**
46	 * Whether `path` names an existing directory the harness can ENTER. The
47	 * search-permission probe matters: `statSync().isDirectory()` is true for a
48	 * mode-600 directory, but a subprocess cwd needs `X_OK` or spawn fails EACCES.
49	 */
50	function isEnterableDirectory(path: string): boolean {
51	  try {
52	    if (!statSync(path).isDirectory()) return false
53	    accessSync(path, constants.X_OK)
54	    return true
55	  } catch {
56	    // statSync/accessSync throw only filesystem access errors here
57	    // (ENOENT/EACCES/ENOTDIR/…), and every one of them means the path cannot
58	    // serve as the child's cwd.
59	    return false
60	  }
61	}
62	
63	/**
64	 * Assert `cwd` can actually host the child: absolute (it doubles as the
65	 * child's workspace identity, and a relative path would be re-anchored to the
66	 * server process's launch directory) and an existing directory (fail here,
67	 * before the process boundary, instead of as an ambiguous spawn ENOENT).
68	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix.
69	 * @param label - which source supplied the value, for the diagnostic.
70	 * @param cwd - the candidate working directory.
71	 * @returns `cwd`, validated.
72	 */
73	export function assertUsableCwd(prefix: string, label: string, cwd: string): string {
74	  if (!isAbsolute(cwd)) {
75	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: ${label} must be an absolute path: ${cwd}`)
76	  }
77	  if (!isEnterableDirectory(cwd)) {
78	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: ${label} is not an accessible directory: ${cwd}`)
79	  }
80	  return cwd
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * Validate a configured `cwd` override ONCE, at plugin load: reject the empty
85	 * string (`path.resolve('')` is the process cwd — it would silently
86	 * reintroduce the launch-directory fallback this resolution removes),
87	 * interpret a relative path against the harness launch directory, and require
88	 * an enterable directory.
89	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix.
90	 * @param cwd - the configured override, or `undefined` when the config omits it.
91	 * @returns the validated absolute override, or `undefined` when omitted.
92	 */
93	export function validateConfiguredCwd(prefix: string, cwd: string | undefined): string | undefined {
94	  if (cwd === undefined) return undefined
95	  if (cwd === '') {
96	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: config cwd must not be empty — omit the key to inherit the parent session cwd`)
97	  }
98	  return assertUsableCwd(prefix, 'config cwd', resolve(cwd))
99	}
100	
101	/**
102	 * Resolve the child's working directory at start: the deployment override
103	 * when configured (already validated at load), else the parent session's
104	 * workspace cwd (validated here, its earliest resolvable point). Fails loud
105	 * when neither exists — falling back to the harness process cwd would
106	 * silently bind the child to the server's launch directory instead of the
107	 * delegating session's workspace (one server process serves many sessions,
108	 * each with its own cwd).
109	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix.
110	 * @param configured - the load-validated override, or `undefined`.
111	 * @param parentCwd - the delegating parent session's workspace cwd, if any.
112	 * @returns the absolute child working directory.
113	 */
114	export function resolveChildCwd(prefix: string, configured: string | undefined, parentCwd: string | undefined): string {
115	  if (configured !== undefined) return configured
116	  if (parentCwd === undefined) {
117	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: no working directory for the child — configure \`cwd\` or delegate from a parent session that has one`)
118	  }
119	  return assertUsableCwd(prefix, 'parent session cwd', parentCwd)
120	}
121	
122	/** Normalize an unknown thrown value to an Error (the catch binding is `unknown`). */
123	function toError(value: unknown): Error {
124	  // The rejecting surfaces (wire clients, spawn failures) only throw
125	  // `Error`s; the `String(value)` arm is a defensive fallback for a non-Error
126	  // throw the typed surfaces cannot produce.
127	  /* v8 ignore next */
128	  return value instanceof Error ? value : new Error(String(value))
129	}
130	
131	/** Inputs to {@link settleRunResult}. */
132	export interface RunResultSettlement {
133	  /** The turn attempt (typically racing local cancellation); returns the terminal result. */
134	  attempt: () => Promise<SubagentResult>
135	  /** Snapshot the provider exposes when cancellation or failure wins settlement. */
136	  collectOutput: () => ContentBlock[]
137	  /** Whether local cancellation settled before the attempt's outcome is observed. */
138	  cancelled: () => boolean
139	  /** Diagnostic sink for a failure flattened to a stop reason; a throw from it is contained. */
140	  onError?: ((error: Error, stopReason: SubagentStopReason) => void) | undefined
141	  /** The request's cancellation signal (the listener is removed at settlement). */
142	  signal: AbortSignal
143	  /** The abort listener registered on {@link signal} at start. */
144	  onAbort: () => void
145	}
146	
147	/**
148	 * Settle an out-of-process run result under the seam contract: `result` never
149	 * rejects after publication. A normally completed or rejected attempt resolves
150	 * as `aborted` when cancellation already settled locally; another rejection is
151	 * flattened to `stopReason: 'error'` through the contained diagnostic sink.
152	 * The abort listener is removed on every path.
153	 * @param parts - the attempt, output snapshot, cancellation state, sink, and signal wiring.
154	 * @returns the terminal result (never a rejection).
155	 */
156	export async function settleRunResult(parts: RunResultSettlement): Promise<SubagentResult> {
157	  try {
158	    const result = await parts.attempt()
159	    return parts.cancelled()
160	      ? { output: parts.collectOutput(), stopReason: 'aborted' }
161	      : result
162	  } catch (error: unknown) {
163	    // Cover a rejection already queued when cancellation arrives.
164	    if (parts.cancelled()) return { output: parts.collectOutput(), stopReason: 'aborted' }
165	    // Flatten post-publication transport failures while preserving diagnostics.
166	    try {
167	      parts.onError?.(toError(error), 'error')
168	    } catch {
169	      // The diagnostic sink cannot reject the run result.
170	    }
171	    return { output: parts.collectOutput(), stopReason: 'error' }
172	  } finally {
173	    parts.signal.removeEventListener('abort', parts.onAbort)
174	  }
175	}
176	
177	/** Inputs to {@link subprocessRunHandle}. */
178	export interface SubprocessRunHandleParts {
179	  /** The parent-scoped run id. */
180	  id: SubagentRun['id']
181	  /** The flattened, never-rejecting result (the seam contract). */
182	  result: Promise<SubagentResult>
183	  /** The request's cancellation signal (the listener is removed on dispose). */
184	  signal: AbortSignal
185	  /** The abort listener registered on {@link signal} at start. */
186	  onAbort: () => void
187	  /** Settle local cancellation so {@link result} resolves without the child. */
188	  requestCancel: () => void
189	  /** Tear the child process down to quiescence (backend-owned ladder). */
190	  teardown: () => Promise<void>
191	}
192	
193	/**
194	 * Publish the seam run handle for an out-of-process child. `dispose()` is
195	 * idempotent (one memoized teardown): it removes the abort listener, settles
196	 * local cancellation — there is no assumption the child cooperates — and then
197	 * awaits the backend's teardown to actual exit.
198	 * @param parts - the run identity, result, cancellation wiring, and teardown.
199	 * @returns the seam run handle (`localAgent` is `undefined` for remote runs).
200	 */
201	export function subprocessRunHandle(parts: SubprocessRunHandleParts): SubagentRun {
202	  let disposal: Promise<void> | undefined
203	  return {
204	    id: parts.id,
205	    localAgent: undefined,
206	    result: parts.result,
207	    dispose(): Promise<void> {
208	      if (disposal !== undefined) return disposal
209	      parts.signal.removeEventListener('abort', parts.onAbort)
210	      parts.requestCancel()
211	      disposal = parts.teardown()
212	      return disposal
213	    },
214	  }
215	}
