1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the scorekeeper: the four `SessionFacts` groups one session
3	 * log folds into, the scoreboard rows and per-environment statistics a batch
4	 * of persisted logs folds into, and the facts-export request and report.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper/types
7	 */
8	
9	import type { BudgetCapId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
10	import type { EnvironmentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
11	import type { GoalPhase } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal/types'
12	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types'
13	import type { TrajectoryRewardBasis, TrajectorySink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories/types'
14	import type { CertificateIsolation, RunExecutor, RunParity, RunVerdict } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
15	
16	/**
17	 * Tamper status of one session: the verdict of its last recorded
18	 * `verification/run`, or `not-instrumented` for a session whose log records no
19	 * run at all, so no verdict states whether the check-owned files changed.
20	 */
21	export type SessionTamper = RunVerdict | 'not-instrumented'
22	
23	/**
24	 * The fields of the `environment/run` stamp the facts keep: the cell identity
25	 * a scoreboard row is keyed by plus the decontamination digest.
26	 */
27	export interface SessionFactsEnvironment {
28	  /** Environment that was run. */
29	  readonly environmentId: EnvironmentId
30	  /** Declared kind of that environment. */
31	  readonly environmentKind: string
32	  /** Whether the environment is reserved for evaluation. */
33	  readonly heldOut: boolean
34	  /** Zero-based repetition of the run inside its batch. */
35	  readonly repetition: number
36	  /** Batch identity the stamp carried, absent for a single run. */
37	  readonly group?: string
38	  /** District the run belonged to, absent for a run outside every district. */
39	  readonly district?: string
40	  /** SHA-256 hex over the prompt, fixture, and check digests; the decontamination key. */
41	  readonly contentSha256: string
42	  /** Provider route the run declared. */
43	  readonly provider: string
44	  /** Provider-owned model id the run declared. */
45	  readonly model: string
46	  /** Isolation the deployment declared for the run's checks. */
47	  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
48	}
49	
50	/** Who ran what, on which route: the identity and provenance the session log carries. */
51	export interface SessionFactsIdentity {
52	  /** The `environment/run` stamp's fields, absent for a session no runner stamped. */
53	  readonly environment?: SessionFactsEnvironment
54	  /** Provider route of the last `request/header`, absent for a session that made no request. */
55	  readonly requestProvider?: string
56	  /** Model id of the last `request/header`, absent for a session that made no request. */
57	  readonly requestModel?: string
58	  /**
59	   * `compositionSha256` of the last `composition/manifest` in the session,
60	   * absent for a session whose log carries none. It addresses the component set
61	   * the agent had in play, so a row carrying it is attributable to one harness
62	   * variant rather than to a route and whatever the harness was that week.
63	   */
64	  readonly compositionSha256?: string
65	}
66	
67	/** {@link SessionFactsIdentity} plus the identity only the persisted session header carries. */
68	export interface PersistedFactsIdentity extends SessionFactsIdentity {
69	  /** Session the facts were folded from. */
70	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
71	  /** Session creation time from the stored header, epoch milliseconds. */
72	  readonly createdAt: number
73	}
74	
75	/** What the session achieved, as its goal, verification, and budget events decided. */
76	export interface SessionFactsOutcome {
77	  /** `1` for a certified completion, `0` for a measured goal without a covering certificate, `null` when no verifier decided. */
78	  readonly reward: 1 | 0 | null
79	  /** How {@link reward} was decided, by the trajectory reward fold's rules. */
80	  readonly rewardBasis: TrajectoryRewardBasis
81	  /** Whether the verification fold holds a certificate covering the current standard revision. */
82	  readonly certified: boolean
83	  /** Standard revision that certificate covers, absent without one. */
84	  readonly certificateRevision?: number
85	  /**
86	   * Executor of the run that certificate cites, absent without one. A
87	   * leaderboard partitions on it: an `agent-reported` certificate is the
88	   * implementer's own account of its checks and can only claim `none`.
89	   */
90	  readonly certificateExecutor?: RunExecutor
91	  /**
92	   * Weighted pass rate of the last recorded run, absent when that run measured
93	   * no cases. It states how much of the measured behaviour the session reached
94	   * and certifies nothing; {@link certified} remains the only completion
95	   * measure, and the two are separate facts that are never merged.
96	   */
97	  readonly parity?: RunParity
98	  /**
99	   * Verdict of the last recorded run, `not-instrumented` when the session
100	   * recorded none. It is the tamper column a publication carries: `passed` and
101	   * `failed` follow from the run's results, while `tampered` says the
102	   * check-owned files changed under the validator and only the run payload
103	   * states it.
104	   */
105	  readonly tamper: SessionTamper
106	  /** `verification/run` events recorded across the session, passing or failing. */
107	  readonly runsRecorded: number
108	  /** Attempt number the last recorded run carried; it restarts at one for each authored standard. */
109	  readonly attempts: number
110	  /** `verification/directive` events recorded across the session. */
111	  readonly directives: number
112	  /** Checks relaxed out of the current standard. */
113	  readonly relaxations: number
114	  /** Durable phase of the current goal, absent before the first create and after a clear. */
115	  readonly goalPhase?: GoalPhase
116	  /** Highest admitted continuation round of the current goal. */
117	  readonly goalRoundsStarted: number
118	  /** Round cap of the current goal, absent without a current goal. */
119	  readonly goalRoundsCap?: number
120	  /** Cap named by the last `budget/breach`, absent for a session that breached none. */
121	  readonly budgetBreachCap?: BudgetCapId
122	}
123	
124	/**
125	 * What the session cost, from its turn, step, usage, and pricing events. Cost
126	 * is read from the `usage/priced` records alone, never recomputed from a
127	 * deployment's current pricing table, so a table edited after the fact cannot
128	 * change what a folded session cost.
129	 */
130	export interface SessionFactsEfficiency {
131	  /** `turn/start` events. */
132	  readonly turns: number
133	  /** `step/start` events. */
134	  readonly steps: number
135	  /** Uncached input tokens summed over every `assistant/message` that reported usage. */
136	  readonly inputTokens: number
137	  /** Output tokens summed over the same messages. */
138	  readonly outputTokens: number
139	  /** Cache-read tokens summed over the same messages. */
140	  readonly cacheReadTokens: number
141	  /** Cache-write tokens summed over the same messages. */
142	  readonly cacheWriteTokens: number
143	  /** Reasoning tokens summed over the same messages. */
144	  readonly reasoningTokens: number
145	  /** Milliseconds between the first and the last event time; `0` for a log of fewer than two events. */
146	  readonly wallMs: number
147	  /** `usage/priced` events: the steps whose price the log states. */
148	  readonly pricedSteps: number
149	  /**
150	   * EUR summed over the `costEur` of those events, absent when any
151	   * `assistant/message` that reported usage has no `usage/priced` for its turn
152	   * and step: a session that ran an unpriced route states no cost rather than
153	   * the lower cost of its priced steps alone. `0` for a session whose log
154	   * carries no usage-bearing message.
155	   */
156	  readonly costEur?: number
157	  /**
158	   * Distinct `pricingDigest` values of those events, in first-seen order. Two
159	   * or more mean the log was priced under more than one table version, so
160	   * {@link costEur} is a sum across pricing tables.
161	   */
162	  readonly pricingDigests: readonly string[]
163	}
164	
165	/** How the session used tools, from its `tool/call` and `tool/result` events. */
166	export interface SessionFactsTools {
167	  /** `tool/call` events. */
168	  readonly toolCalls: number
169	  /** `tool/call` events per registered tool name, in first-call order. */
170	  readonly toolCallsByName: Readonly<Record<string, number>>
171	  /** `tool/result` events whose model-facing block reported an error. */
172	  readonly toolErrors: number
173	  /** Tool errors whose recorded `error.code` is the timeout policy's `TOOL_TIMEOUT`. */
174	  readonly toolTimeouts: number
175	  /** Tool errors whose recorded `error.code` is the tool runtime's `ABORTED` or `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH`. */
176	  readonly toolAborts: number
177	}
178	
179	/** One session log folded into the four fact groups. */
180	export interface SessionFacts {
181	  readonly identity: SessionFactsIdentity
182	  readonly outcome: SessionFactsOutcome
183	  readonly efficiency: SessionFactsEfficiency
184	  readonly tools: SessionFactsTools
185	}
186	
187	/** One persisted session's facts, carrying the identity its stored header adds. */
188	export interface SessionFactsRecord extends SessionFacts {
189	  readonly identity: PersistedFactsIdentity
190	}
191	
192	/** Which persisted sessions a scoreboard folds. */
193	export interface LeaderboardFilter {
194	  /** Sessions to fold; absent folds every persisted session. */
195	  readonly sessions?: readonly SessionId[]
196	  /** Only sessions whose stamp carries this batch identity. */
197	  readonly group?: string
198	  /** Only held-out (`true`) or only training-eligible (`false`) sessions. */
199	  readonly heldOut?: boolean
200	}
201	
202	/** One unbiased pass@k estimate over the repetition batches of one scoreboard row. */
203	export interface PassAtK {
204	  /** Repetitions drawn per estimate. */
205	  readonly k: number
206	  /** Mean of `1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k)` over the batches of at least `k` sessions. */
207	  readonly value: number
208	  /** Batches that held at least `k` sessions and therefore contributed. */
209	  readonly groups: number
210	}
211	
212	/**
213	 * Measured difficulty of one environment under one model route, estimated from
214	 * the repetitions of each batch the row's sessions belong to.
215	 */
216	export interface EnvironmentStats {
217	  /** Distinct batch identities among the row's sessions. */
218	  readonly groups: number
219	  /** Sessions whose stamp carried a batch identity. */
220	  readonly samples: number
221	  /** One estimate per configured `k`, ascending; a `k` no batch reached is absent. */
222	  readonly passAtK: readonly PassAtK[]
223	}
224	
225	/**
226	 * One scoreboard row: one model route on one environment at one isolation
227	 * level, one side of the held-out split, and one district. Rows never average
228	 * across isolation, the split, or districts; all three are columns a consumer
229	 * partitions by, and a publication that withholds a district drops whole rows.
230	 */
231	export interface ScoreboardRow {
232	  readonly provider: string
233	  readonly model: string
234	  readonly environmentId: EnvironmentId
235	  readonly environmentKind: string
236	  readonly heldOut: boolean
237	  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
238	  /** District every session of the row was stamped with, absent for a row outside every district. */
239	  readonly district?: string
240	  /** Sessions that recorded at least one `verification/run`. */
241	  readonly runs: number
242	  /** Sessions that ended without recording one; they are exactly the row's not-instrumented sessions. */
243	  readonly errors: number
244	  /**
245	   * Sessions whose last recorded run carried the `tampered` verdict. A row
246	   * whose {@link runs} is zero states no tamper status at all, because a
247	   * session that recorded no run carries no verdict to read.
248	   */
249	  readonly tampered: number
250	  /**
251	   * `compositionSha256` every session of the row states, absent when a session
252	   * states none or two disagree. A digest covering only part of a row would
253	   * attribute the whole row to a composition that did not run all of it.
254	   */
255	  readonly compositionSha256?: string
256	  /**
257	   * Distinct certificate executors across the row's certified sessions, in
258	   * first-appearance order. Empty for a row that certified nothing; two or more
259	   * mean the row's certificates disagree, so no single executor may be
260	   * published beside its {@link certificateRate}.
261	   */
262	  readonly certificateExecutors: readonly RunExecutor[]
263	  /** Sessions holding a certificate. */
264	  readonly certified: number
265	  /** `certified / runs`, `0` without runs. */
266	  readonly certificateRate: number
267	  /**
268	   * Mean `weightPassed / weightTotal` over the row's sessions that carry a
269	   * parity, absent when none does; every such session counts once, so a
270	   * session sampled by more cases does not weigh more. It is a column beside
271	   * {@link certificateRate}, never merged with it and never ranked against it.
272	   */
273	  readonly parity?: number
274	  /** Mean `runsRecorded` over the sessions with runs, `0` without runs. */
275	  readonly attemptsMean: number
276	  /** Input tokens summed over every session of the row, the errored ones included. */
277	  readonly inputTokens: number
278	  /** Output tokens summed over the same sessions. */
279	  readonly outputTokens: number
280	  /**
281	   * Mean `costEur` over the row's certified sessions, absent when the row
282	   * certified nothing and absent when any certified session of the row states
283	   * no cost, so a published figure never averages an unpriced session as free.
284	   */
285	  readonly costEurPerCertified?: number

117	/** Whether the outcome group folds from this event. */
118	function isOutcomeEvent(event: SessionEvent): boolean {
119	  switch (event.type) {
120	    case 'goal/change':
121	    case 'verification/standard':
122	    case 'verification/relaxation':
123	    case 'verification/run':
124	    case 'verification/certificate':
125	    case 'verification/directive':
126	    case 'budget/breach':
127	      return true
128	    // An admitted continuation round is a user message; the goal fold counts it.
129	    case 'user/message':

136	/** The cap of the last recorded breach, absent when the events hold none. */
137	function breachCap(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): Pick<SessionFactsOutcome, 'budgetBreachCap'> {

139	  for (const event of events) {

145	/**
146	 * Fold the outcome group from the goal, verification, and budget events.
147	 * @param events - the kept outcome events in sequence order.
148	 * @returns the outcome group.
149	 * @throws when a kept event violates the strict goal or verification stream.
150	 */
151	function foldOutcome(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): SessionFactsOutcome {
152	  const reward = foldTrajectoryReward(events)

177	/** Replace the identity group. */

197	/**
198	 * Replace the pricing state and rebuild the three efficiency fields it decides.
199	 * `costEur` is rebuilt rather than merged, so a usage-bearing step that arrives

214	/** Add one durable step price to the pricing state. */

254	/**

268	    cacheWriteTokens: totals.cacheWriteTokens + (usage.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0),

270	  })

277	/** Count one tool result that reported an error, classified by its recorded code. */

280	  if (block.isError !== true) return state

291	/**
292	 * Fold one event into the accumulator.
293	 * @param state - the accumulator covering every prior event.
294	 * @param event - the next event in sequence order.
295	 * @returns the next accumulator; every event moves the log's time span, so the reference always changes.
296	 * @throws when the event is a goal or verification change the strict folds reject.
297	 */
298	export function applySessionFacts(state: SessionFactsState, event: SessionEvent): SessionFactsState {

300	  if (isOutcomeEvent(event)) {

302	    return { ...timed, outcomeEvents, facts: { ...timed.facts, outcome: foldOutcome(outcomeEvents) } }

304	  switch (event.type) {
305	    case 'turn/start':
306	      return withEfficiency(timed, { turns: timed.facts.efficiency.turns + 1 })
307	    case 'step/start':
308	      return withEfficiency(timed, { steps: timed.facts.efficiency.steps + 1 })
309	    case 'assistant/message':
310	      return withUsage(timed, event)
311	    case 'usage/priced':
312	      return withPrice(timed, event)
313	    case 'environment/run':
314	      return withStamp(timed, event)
315	    case 'request/header':
316	      return withIdentity(timed, {
317	        requestProvider: event.data.header.config.provider,
318	        requestModel: event.data.header.config.model,
319	      })
320	    case 'composition/manifest':
321	      return withIdentity(timed, { compositionSha256: event.data.compositionSha256 })
322	    case 'tool/call': {
323	      const tools = timed.facts.tools
324	      const calls = tools.toolCallsByName[event.data.name] ?? 0
325	      return withTools(timed, {
326	        toolCalls: tools.toolCalls + 1,
327	        toolCallsByName: { ...tools.toolCallsByName, [event.data.name]: calls + 1 },
328	      })
329	    }
330	    case 'tool/result':
331	      return withToolResult(timed, event)
332	    // SessionEventMap is merge-extensible: every other event moves only the time span.
333	    default:
334	      return timed
335	  }
336	}

338	/**
339	 * Fold a whole session log into its accumulator.

343	 */
344	export function foldSessionFactsState(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): SessionFactsState {
345	  let state = emptySessionFactsState()
346	  for (const event of events) state = applySessionFacts(state, event)
347	  return state

359	  return { ...facts, identity: { sessionId: meta.id, createdAt: meta.createdAt, ...facts.identity } }

71	 * concatenated so no field value can spell a separator and merge two cells —
72	 * two districts above all — into one row.

79	    environment.isolation,
80	    environment.heldOut,

85	/**
86	 * Unbiased pass@k over one batch: the chance that a draw of `k` of its `n`
87	 * sessions holds at least one certified session, `1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k)`
88	 * evaluated as a product so no factorial overflows.
89	 * @param n - sessions in the batch, at least `k`.
90	 * @param c - how many of them certified.
91	 * @param k - repetitions drawn.
92	 * @returns the estimate between `0` and `1`.
93	 */
94	export function unbiasedPassAtK(n: number, c: number, k: number): number {
95	  if (n - c < k) return 1
96	  let miss = 1
97	  for (let index = 0; index < k; index += 1) miss *= (n - c - index) / (n - index)
98	  return 1 - miss
99	}
100	
101	/** Estimate pass@k for every configured `k` a batch of the row reached. */
102	function statsOf(batches: ReadonlyMap<string, Batch>, ks: readonly number[]): EnvironmentStats {
103	  let samples = 0
104	  for (const batch of batches.values()) samples += batch.samples
105	  const passAtK: PassAtK[] = []
106	  for (const k of ks) {
107	    let total = 0
108	    let groups = 0
109	    for (const batch of batches.values()) {
110	      if (batch.samples < k) continue
111	      total += unbiasedPassAtK(batch.samples, batch.certified, k)
112	      groups += 1
113	    }
114	    if (groups > 0) passAtK.push({ k, value: total / groups, groups })
115	  }
116	  return { groups: batches.size, samples, passAtK }
117	}

119	/** Whether one stamped session passes the filter's group and held-out conditions. */

122	  return filter.heldOut === undefined || environment.heldOut === filter.heldOut

130	function agreeComposition(row: RowAccumulator, digest: string | undefined, first: boolean): void {
131	  if (digest === undefined || (!first && row.compositionSha256 !== digest)) row.compositionMixed = true
132	  else row.compositionSha256 = digest

154	    executors: new Set<RunExecutor>(),
155	    batches: new Map<string, Batch>(),
156	  }
157	  const first = !rows.has(key)
158	  rows.set(key, row)
159	  const outcome = record.outcome
160	  const efficiency = record.efficiency
161	  if (outcome.runsRecorded === 0) row.errors += 1
162	  else {
163	    row.runs += 1
164	    row.attemptSum += outcome.runsRecorded
165	  }
166	  if (outcome.tamper === 'tampered') row.tampered += 1
167	  agreeComposition(row, record.identity.compositionSha256, first)
168	  if (outcome.certified) {
169	    row.certified += 1
170	    /* v8 ignore next -- a certified session states the executor of the run its certificate cites. */
171	    if (outcome.certificateExecutor !== undefined) row.executors.add(outcome.certificateExecutor)
172	    if (efficiency.costEur === undefined) row.uncostedCertified += 1
173	    else row.certifiedCostEur += efficiency.costEur
174	  }
175	  if (outcome.parity !== undefined) {
176	    row.parityRateSum += outcome.parity.weightPassed / outcome.parity.weightTotal
177	    row.paritySessions += 1
178	  }
179	  row.inputTokens += efficiency.inputTokens
180	  row.outputTokens += efficiency.outputTokens
181	  for (const digest of efficiency.pricingDigests) row.digests.add(digest)
182	  if (environment.group === undefined) return
183	  const batch = row.batches.get(environment.group) ?? { samples: 0, certified: 0 }
184	  row.batches.set(environment.group, batch)
185	  batch.samples += 1
186	  if (outcome.certified) batch.certified += 1
187	}

189	/** Close one accumulator into its row. */
190	function finish(row: RowAccumulator, ks: readonly number[]): ScoreboardRow {
191	  return {
192	    provider: row.environment.provider,
193	    model: row.environment.model,
194	    environmentId: row.environment.environmentId,
195	    environmentKind: row.environment.environmentKind,
196	    heldOut: row.environment.heldOut,
197	    isolation: row.environment.isolation,
198	    ...row.environment.district === undefined ? {} : { district: row.environment.district },
199	    runs: row.runs,
200	    errors: row.errors,
201	    tampered: row.tampered,
202	    ...row.compositionSha256 === undefined || row.compositionMixed
203	      ? {}
204	      : { compositionSha256: row.compositionSha256 },
205	    certificateExecutors: [...row.executors],
206	    certified: row.certified,
207	    certificateRate: row.runs === 0 ? 0 : row.certified / row.runs,
208	    ...row.paritySessions === 0 ? {} : { parity: row.parityRateSum / row.paritySessions },
209	    attemptsMean: row.runs === 0 ? 0 : row.attemptSum / row.runs,
210	    inputTokens: row.inputTokens,
211	    outputTokens: row.outputTokens,
212	    ...row.certified > 0 && row.uncostedCertified === 0
213	      ? { costEurPerCertified: row.certifiedCostEur / row.certified }
214	      : {},
215	    pricingDigests: [...row.digests],
216	    stats: statsOf(row.batches, ks),
217	  }
218	}

220	/**
221	 * Fold session facts into scoreboard rows.
222	 * @param records - one facts record per session, in the order the rows appear.
223	 * @param filter - the group and held-out conditions a stamped record must meet.
224	 * @param ks - the pass@k draws to estimate, ascending.
225	 * @returns the rows plus the counts of excluded and unstamped records.
226	 */
227	export function foldScoreboard(
228	  records: readonly SessionFactsRecord[],
229	  filter: LeaderboardFilter,
230	  ks: readonly number[],
231	): ScoreboardFold {
232	  const rows = new Map<string, RowAccumulator>()
233	  let excluded = 0
234	  let unstamped = 0
235	  for (const record of records) {
236	    const environment = record.identity.environment
237	    if (environment === undefined) {
238	      unstamped += 1
239	      continue
240	    }
241	    if (!matches(filter, environment)) {
242	      excluded += 1
243	      continue
244	    }
245	    accumulate(rows, record, environment)
246	  }
247	  return { rows: [...rows.values()].map(row => finish(row, ks)), excluded, unstamped }
248	}

50	/** SHA-256 hex digest of one UTF-8 string. */

55	/**
56	 * Field-ordered tuple of one check, so the inventory digest does not depend on
57	 * the author's object key order. A check without cases digests exactly the
58	 * three fields every check has always carried.
59	 */
60	function checkTuple(check: AuthoredCheck): unknown[] {
61	  const head = [check.id, check.outcome, check.run]
62	  const { cases, caseBodies, treeScope } = check
63	  if (cases === undefined && caseBodies === undefined && treeScope === undefined) return head
64	  return [
65	    ...head,
66	    treeScope ?? null,
67	    cases === undefined ? null : [cases.count, cases.weightTotal, cases.sha256],
68	    caseBodies === undefined ? null : caseBodiesSha256(caseBodies),

72	/**

74	 * authored order (case bodies included), the caller-computed fixture digest,
75	 * and the combined key.
76	 * @param environment - the task and checks to hash.
77	 * @param fixtureSha256 - digest of the fixture files, absent for a task without a fixture.
78	 * @returns the four digests; identical inputs give identical digests.

80	export function environmentContentHashes(
81	  environment: Pick<EnvironmentDefinition, 'task' | 'checks'>,
82	  fixtureSha256?: string,
83	): EnvironmentContentHashes {
84	  const promptSha256 = sha256(environment.task.prompt)
85	  const checksSha256 = sha256(JSON.stringify(environment.checks.map(checkTuple)))
86	  const contentSha256 = sha256([promptSha256, fixtureSha256 ?? '', checksSha256].join('\n'))
87	  return { promptSha256, checksSha256, ...fixtureSha256 === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256 }, contentSha256 }
88	}

90	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {

94	/** Require one non-empty string field of a durable stamp. */

101	/** Require one SHA-256 hex field of a durable stamp. */

103	  const field = stampText(value, key)
104	  if (!HEX_64.test(field)) throw new Error(`environment/run ${key} must be a SHA-256 hex digest`)

108	/** Require a durable stamp's sampling seed to be a value a provider could have been asked for. */

114	/**

117	 * @param value - candidate seed.
118	 * @returns whether the value can be sent as a seed and written into a stamp.

120	export function isSeed(value: unknown): value is number {
121	  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 0

124	/**
125	 * Decode a value that declares itself as an environment run stamp. Unrelated
126	 * values return `undefined`; a malformed stamp fails replay loudly, as every
127	 * durable payload does at the log boundary.
128	 * @param value - candidate durable payload.
129	 * @returns the validated stamp, or `undefined` for another value kind.
130	 */
131	export function decodeEnvironmentRun(value: unknown): EnvironmentRunStamp | undefined {
132	  if (!isRecord(value) || value['kind'] !== 'environment/run') return undefined
133	  if (value['version'] !== ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION) {
134	    throw new Error(`unsupported environment/run version ${String(value['version'])}`)
135	  }
136	  const heldOut = value['heldOut']
137	  if (typeof heldOut !== 'boolean') throw new Error('environment/run heldOut must be a boolean')
138	  const repetition = value['repetition']
139	  if (typeof repetition !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(repetition) || repetition < 0) {

141	  }
142	  const model = value['model']
143	  if (!isRecord(model)) throw new Error('environment/run model must be a record')

147	  }
148	  const fixture = value['fixtureSha256'] === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256: stampHex(value, 'fixtureSha256') }
149	  const group = value['group'] === undefined ? {} : { group: stampText(value, 'group') }
150	  const district = value['district'] === undefined ? {} : { district: stampText(value, 'district') }
151	  const policyVersion = value['policyVersion'] === undefined ? {} : { policyVersion: stampText(value, 'policyVersion') }
152	  const seed = value['seed'] === undefined ? {} : { seed: stampSeed(value['seed']) }

154	    kind: 'environment/run',
155	    version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
156	    environmentId: EnvironmentId(stampText(value, 'environmentId')),
157	    environmentKind: stampText(value, 'environmentKind'),
158	    heldOut,
159	    promptSha256: stampHex(value, 'promptSha256'),
160	    checksSha256: stampHex(value, 'checksSha256'),
161	    ...fixture,
162	    contentSha256: stampHex(value, 'contentSha256'),
163	    repetition,
164	    ...group,
165	    ...district,
166	    ...policyVersion,
167	    ...seed,
168	    model: { provider: stampText(model, 'provider'), model: stampText(model, 'model') },
169	    isolation: isolation as EnvironmentRunStamp['isolation'],
170	  }
171	}

233	/** Words one prompt is shingled into: each run of non-alphanumeric characters is one separator. */
234	const WORD_SEPARATOR = /[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u
235	
236	/** Words per shingle. Five is long enough that ordinary task phrasing does not collide by itself. */
237	const SHINGLE_SIZE = 5
238	
239	/**
240	 * Word shingles of one prompt, normalized as the admission rule normalizes:
241	 * lower-cased, punctuation replaced by separators, and the resulting whitespace
242	 * collapsed away. A prompt shorter than one shingle contributes its whole word
243	 * list as a single shingle, so two identical short prompts still score 1.
244	 */
245	function promptShingles(prompt: string): ReadonlySet<string> {
246	  const words = prompt.toLowerCase().split(WORD_SEPARATOR).filter(word => word !== '')
247	  if (words.length === 0) return new Set()
248	  if (words.length < SHINGLE_SIZE) return new Set([words.join(' ')])
249	  const shingles = new Set<string>()
250	  for (let start = 0; start + SHINGLE_SIZE <= words.length; start += 1) {
251	    shingles.add(words.slice(start, start + SHINGLE_SIZE).join(' '))
252	  }
253	  return shingles
254	}

256	/**
257	 * Jaccard similarity of two shingle sets: shared shingles over all shingles.
258	 * Two empty sets are identical rather than undefined, which keeps an empty
259	 * prompt from silently admitting beside another empty one.
260	 */
261	function jaccard(a: ReadonlySet<string>, b: ReadonlySet<string>): number {
262	  if (a.size === 0 && b.size === 0) return 1
263	  let shared = 0
264	  for (const shingle of a) if (b.has(shingle)) shared += 1
265	  return shared / (a.size + b.size - shared)
266	}

390	  /**

392	   * the returned disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the entry.
393	   * @param definition - complete environment definition.
394	   * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id.
395	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentError} when the id is already registered, the
396	   *   definition declares no checks, two checks share an id, an immutable
397	   *   path is not a normalized workspace-relative path, the task reference is
398	   *   missing on a `recreation` environment or is not a directory inside the
399	   *   fixture, or a configured near-duplicate threshold refuses the prompt

406	    assertChecks(definition)
407	    assertImmutable(definition)
408	    assertReference(definition)
409	    this.assertNotNearDuplicate(definition)

411	    this.environments.set(stored.id, stored)

417	  /**

421	   * equally contaminating whichever side is registered second.

423	  private assertNotNearDuplicate(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): void {

425	    if (threshold === undefined) return

427	    if (nearest === undefined || nearest.similarity < threshold) return

429	    throw new EnvironmentError(
430	      `environment "${definition.id}" near-duplicates ${opposite} environment "${nearest.environment}": word ${SHINGLE_SIZE}-gram Jaccard similarity ${nearest.similarity} reaches the ${threshold} admission threshold`,

447	  /** The most similar registered environment on one side of the held-out split. */
448	  private nearest(prompt: string, heldOut: boolean): NearestEnvironment | undefined {
449	    const candidate = promptShingles(prompt)
450	    let nearest: NearestEnvironment | undefined

26	/** The districts and held-out split one fold keeps out of its public rows. */

28	  /** Districts whose rows never reach the public page. */
29	  readonly districts: readonly string[]
30	  /** Whether held-out rows are withheld as well. */
31	  readonly heldOut: boolean

36	  readonly published: readonly ScoreboardRow[]
37	  readonly districtRows: number
38	  readonly districtSessions: number
39	  readonly heldOutRows: number
40	  readonly heldOutSessions: number

43	/** Sessions one row folded, the errored ones included. */
44	function sessionsOf(row: ScoreboardRow): number {
45	  return row.runs + row.errors

48	/**
49	 * Split scoreboard rows into the published ones and the withheld counts. A row
50	 * withheld for both reasons is counted under its district, which is checked
51	 * first; the row key carries both dimensions, so every session of a withheld
52	 * row is withheld and no withheld session can reach a published row.
53	 * @param rows - every row the scoreboard folded, in fold order.
54	 * @param rule - the districts and held-out split to withhold.
55	 * @returns the published rows in fold order, and the rows and sessions dropped per reason.
56	 */
57	export function withhold(rows: readonly ScoreboardRow[], rule: WithholdRule): WithholdSplit {
58	  const published: ScoreboardRow[] = []
59	  let districtRows = 0
60	  let districtSessions = 0
61	  let heldOutRows = 0
62	  let heldOutSessions = 0
63	  for (const row of rows) {
64	    if (row.district !== undefined && rule.districts.includes(row.district)) {
65	      districtRows += 1
66	      districtSessions += sessionsOf(row)
67	      continue
68	    }
69	    if (rule.heldOut && row.heldOut) {
70	      heldOutRows += 1
71	      heldOutSessions += sessionsOf(row)
72	      continue
73	    }
74	    published.push(row)
75	  }
76	  return { published, districtRows, districtSessions, heldOutRows, heldOutSessions }
77	}

81	 * serialized rather than concatenated so no field value can spell a separator.
82	 */

84	  return JSON.stringify([
85	    row.provider,
86	    row.model,
87	    row.environmentId,
88	    row.isolation,
89	    row.heldOut,
90	    row.district ?? null,
91	  ])

96	 * scoreboard's own order is the order its session store listed the sessions in,
97	 * which no backend promises to keep, so an unordered page would reshuffle
98	 * between folds that measured the same thing.
99	 * @param rows - the published rows in fold order.
100	 * @returns the same rows in the page's stable order.
101	 */
102	export function orderRows(rows: readonly ScoreboardRow[]): readonly ScoreboardRow[] {
103	  return [...rows].sort((left, right) => (sortKey(left) < sortKey(right) ? -1 : 1))
104	}

111	/**
112	 * Keep the experiment results whose two arm routes both appear in the published
113	 * rows. A verdict about a route the page withholds or never folded publishes no
114	 * ranking, so a ranking is never the only evidence of a session.
115	 * @param experiments - the results a caller holds from its own runs.
116	 * @param rows - the published rows, whose routes are the ones a ranking may name.
117	 * @returns the rankable results in caller order.
118	 */
119	export function rankable(
120	  experiments: readonly ExperimentResult[],
121	  rows: readonly ScoreboardRow[],
122	): readonly ExperimentResult[] {
123	  const routes = new Set(rows.map(row => routeKey(row.provider, row.model)))
124	  return experiments.filter((experiment) => {
125	    const { baseline, candidate } = experiment.arms
126	    return routes.has(routeKey(baseline.model.provider, baseline.model.model))
127	      && routes.has(routeKey(candidate.model.provider, candidate.model.model))
128	  })
129	}

134	  return row.tampered > 0 ? 'tampered' : 'none'

141	 */
142	function costOf(row: ScoreboardRow): Pick<ObservatoryPublishedRow, 'costEurPerCertified' | 'pricingDigest'> {
143	  const [digest, ...rest] = row.pricingDigests
144	  if (digest === undefined || rest.length > 0 || row.costEurPerCertified === undefined) return {}
145	  return { costEurPerCertified: row.costEurPerCertified, pricingDigest: digest }
146	}

150	 * @param row - one published scoreboard row.
151	 * @returns the honest column set, with the cost and tamper rules already applied.
152	 */
153	export function publishRow(row: ScoreboardRow): ObservatoryPublishedRow {
154	  return {
155	    provider: row.provider,
156	    model: row.model,
157	    environmentId: row.environmentId,
158	    environmentKind: row.environmentKind,
159	    ...row.district === undefined ? {} : { district: row.district },
160	    heldOut: row.heldOut,
161	    isolation: row.isolation,
162	    certificateExecutors: row.certificateExecutors,
163	    ...row.compositionSha256 === undefined ? {} : { compositionSha256: row.compositionSha256 },
164	    tamper: tamperOf(row),
165	    tampered: row.tampered,
166	    runs: row.runs,
167	    errors: row.errors,
168	    certified: row.certified,
169	    resolved: row.certificateRate,
170	    ...row.parity === undefined ? {} : { parity: row.parity },
171	    ...costOf(row),
172	  }
173	}

207	  snapshot: ObservatorySnapshot,
208	  now: number,

210	): ObservatoryDocument {

213	    version: OBSERVATORY_DOCUMENT_VERSION,
214	    stale,
215	    foldedAt: snapshot.foldedAt,

217	    refreshIntervalMs: snapshot.refreshIntervalMs,
218	    staleAfterMs,

220	    withheld: snapshot.withheld,
221	    rankings: stale ? [] : snapshot.experiments.map(publishRanking),
222	  }

1	/**
2	 * Freezing one shift: the content digest computed before any cell runs, the
3	 * shift instance id derived from it and the slot time, and the cell
4	 * enumeration both the ledger and the fleet run take.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts/plan
7	 */
8	
9	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
10	import type { FleetCell } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet/types'
11	import type { ShiftPlan } from './types.ts'
12	
13	/**
14	 * Group namespace this package owns. A stamp `group` starting with it names a
15	 * shift, so no other producer may mint one.
16	 */
17	export const SHIFT_ID_PREFIX = 'shift-'
18	
19	/** Self-declared version of the digested plan fields; a change to what they cover changes it. */
20	const SHIFT_PLAN_VERSION = 2
21	
22	const SHIFT_ID_PATTERN = new RegExp(`^${SHIFT_ID_PREFIX}([0-9a-f]{64})-(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`)
23	
24	/**
25	 * Content digest of the fields that decide what a shift runs: the district,
26	 * the environment ids sorted by code unit so a registry listing order cannot
27	 * change the identity, the model routes in listing order because the fleet
28	 * enumerates cells in it, the repetition count, the policy version and base
29	 * seed the cells sample under, and the token ceiling. The workspace root, the
30	 * cadence, and the spend window are deployment choices and stay out: they
31	 * decide what a deployment pays for, not what the shift runs.
32	 * @param plan - the frozen plan to digest.
33	 * @returns the SHA-256 hex digest; identical inputs give identical digests.
34	 */
35	export function shiftDigest(plan: ShiftPlan): string {
36	  const content = JSON.stringify({
37	    version: SHIFT_PLAN_VERSION,
38	    district: plan.district,
39	    environments: [...plan.environments].sort(),
40	    models: plan.models.map(model => [model.provider, model.model]),
41	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
42	    policyVersion: plan.policyVersion ?? null,
43	    seed: plan.seed ?? null,
44	    tokenCeiling: plan.tokenCeiling ?? null,
45	  })
46	  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
47	}
48	
49	/**
50	 * Identity of one shift instance, and the stamp `group` every cell of it
51	 * carries. Two processes that compute the same slot compute the same identity
52	 * without counting anything, so a restart resumes a shift instead of minting a
53	 * second one.
54	 * @param digest - the frozen plan digest.
55	 * @param scheduledAt - the slot time in epoch milliseconds.
56	 * @returns `shift-<digest>-<scheduledAt>`.
57	 */
58	export function shiftId(digest: string, scheduledAt: number): string {
59	  return `${SHIFT_ID_PREFIX}${digest}-${scheduledAt}`
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * Read an id minted by {@link shiftId}.
64	 * @param id - a stamp `group` or a shift session id.
65	 * @returns the digest and slot time, or `undefined` for an id outside this
66	 *   package's namespace or malformed inside it.
67	 */
68	export function parseShiftId(id: string): { digest: string; scheduledAt: number } | undefined {
69	  const match = SHIFT_ID_PATTERN.exec(id)
70	  if (match === null) return undefined
71	  return { digest: match[1] as string, scheduledAt: Number(match[2]) }
72	}
73	
74	/**
75	 * Every cell of a frozen plan, in the order the fleet enumerates them:
76	 * environment-major, then model route, then repetition from zero.
77	 * @param plan - the frozen plan to enumerate.
78	 * @returns the cells in plan order.
79	 */
80	export function shiftCells(plan: ShiftPlan): FleetCell[] {
81	  const cells: FleetCell[] = []
82	  for (const environment of plan.environments) {
83	    for (const model of plan.models) {
84	      for (let repetition = 0; repetition < plan.repetitions; repetition += 1) cells.push({ environment, model, repetition })
85	    }
86	  }
87	  return cells
88	}

90	/**
91	 * The slot a district opens next.
92	 *
93	 * Slots form an arithmetic sequence anchored on the district's previous
94	 * `shift/start`, so a restart neither drifts nor doubles a slot; slots that
95	 * passed while no process ran are skipped rather than caught up, and the hole
96	 * stays visible from the arithmetic. A district with no slot yet opens one now
97	 * when the deployment asked to start immediately, and one interval out
98	 * otherwise.
99	 * @param previous - the district's previous slot time, absent when it has none.
100	 * @param intervalMs - milliseconds between consecutive slots.
101	 * @param now - the current epoch milliseconds.
102	 * @param startImmediately - whether a district without a slot opens one now.
103	 * @returns the next slot time in epoch milliseconds.
104	 */
105	export function nextSlotAt(
106	  previous: number | undefined,
107	  intervalMs: number,
108	  now: number,
109	  startImmediately: boolean,
110	): number {
111	  if (previous === undefined) return startImmediately ? now : now + intervalMs
112	  const elapsed = now - previous
113	  const skipped = elapsed < 0 ? 0 : Math.floor(elapsed / intervalMs)
114	  return previous + (skipped + 1) * intervalMs
115	}

236	    for (const ledger of scan.ledgers) {
237	      if (this.stopping) return
238	      if (ledger.end === undefined) await this.resume(ledger, scan.stamped)
239	    }
240	    for (const district of this.config.districts) {
241	      if (this.stopping) return
242	      await this.openDistrict(district, previousSlot(scan.ledgers, district.district))
243	    }
244	  }

246	  /** Arm the district's cadence, then run the slot it already owes. */
247	  private async openDistrict(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, previous: number | undefined): Promise<void> {
248	    const at = nextSlotAt(previous, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), this.config.startImmediately)
249	    if (at > Date.now()) {
250	      this.arm(district, at)
251	      return
252	    }
253	    this.arm(district, nextSlotAt(at, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), false))
254	    await this.slot(district, at)
255	  }
256	
257	  /**
258	   * Replace one district's cadence timer with one firing at `at`. Each firing
259	   * arms the next slot before it runs this one, so slots keep arriving on the
260	   * cadence and a slot that lands on a still-running shift is refused rather
261	   * than delayed into it.
262	   */
263	  private arm(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, at: number): void {
264	    void this.timers.get(district.district)?.()
265	    const disarm = this.ctx.effect(() => {
266	      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
267	        this.arm(district, nextSlotAt(at, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), false))
268	        // A slot that cannot be frozen must not take the loop down with it: the
269	        // next slot is already armed and the failure is the operator's signal.
270	        void this.slot(district, at).catch((error: unknown) => {
271	          this.ctx.logger.error(`district "${district.district}" slot ${at} failed: ${String(error)}`)
272	        })
273	      }, Math.max(0, at - Date.now()))
274	      return () => {
275	        clearTimeout(timer)
276	      }
277	    }, `shifts.cadence(${district.district})`)
278	    this.timers.set(district.district, disarm)
279	  }
280	
281	  /** Freeze one slot and either refuse it or run it, keeping one shift per district in flight. */
282	  private async slot(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, scheduledAt: number): Promise<void> {
283	    const plan = this.freeze(district)
284	    const digest = shiftDigest(plan)
285	    const id = shiftId(digest, scheduledAt)
286	    if (this.running.has(plan.district)) {
287	      await this.skip(id, { digest, scheduledAt, reason: 'overlap' })
288	      return
289	    }
290	    const inFlight = this.runSlot(district, plan, digest, id, scheduledAt)
291	      .finally(() => {
292	        this.running.delete(plan.district)
293	      })
294	    this.running.set(plan.district, inFlight)
295	    await inFlight
296	  }
297	
298	  /** Refuse the slot for its district's spend window, or open the shift and drive it. */
299	  private async runSlot(
300	    district: ShiftDistrictConfig,
301	    plan: ShiftPlan,
302	    digest: string,
303	    id: string,
304	    scheduledAt: number,
305	  ): Promise<void> {
306	    const window = district.spendWindow
307	    if (window !== undefined) {
308	      const scan = await this.scan()
309	      const spent = windowSpend(scan.ledgers, plan.district, window.windowMs, Date.now())
310	      if (spent >= window.maxTokens) {
311	        await this.skip(id, { digest, scheduledAt, reason: 'spend-window' })
312	        return
313	      }
314	    }
315	    const cells = shiftCells(plan)
316	    const session = this.ctx.sessions.prepare(SessionId(id), { meta: { cwd: this.config.workspaceRoot } })
317	    await this.publish(session, async () => {
318	      session.append('shift/start', { shiftId: id, digest, plan, scheduledAt })
319	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
320	      await this.drive(session, id, plan, cells, 0)
321	    })
322	  }

324	  /** Record one refused slot as its own session, holding that one event. */
325	  private async skip(id: string, skipped: ShiftSkipped): Promise<void> {
326	    const session = this.ctx.sessions.prepare(SessionId(id), { meta: { cwd: this.config.workspaceRoot } })
327	    await this.publish(session, () => {
328	      session.append('shift/skipped', skipped)
329	    })
330	  }

332	  /** Record the orphans of an interrupted process, then run what never started. */
333	  private async resume(ledger: ShiftLedger, stamped: readonly StampedCell[]): Promise<void> {
334	    const { plan, shiftId: id } = ledger.start
335	    const cells = shiftCells(plan)
336	    const split = splitPending(cells, ledger, stamped)
337	    const preparation = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.prepare(ledger.sessionId)
338	    const { session } = preparation
339	    try {
340	      await this.publish(session, async () => {
341	        for (const orphan of split.orphans) {
342	          session.append('shift/cell', {
343	            shiftId: id,
344	            cell: orphan.cell,
345	            sessionId: orphan.sessionId,
346	            outcome: { kind: 'interrupted' },
347	          })
348	        }
349	        session.append('shift/resume', { shiftId: id, done: split.done, pending: split.pending })
350	        await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
351	        await this.drive(session, id, plan, split.pending, shiftSpend(stamped, id))
352	      })
353	    } finally {
354	      preparation[Symbol.dispose]()
355	    }
356	  }
357	
358	  /**
359	   * Run the pending cells of one shift through the fleet, writing one
360	   * `shift/cell` per announced cell, and close the ledger.
361	   */
362	  private async drive(
363	    session: Session,
364	    id: string,
365	    plan: ShiftPlan,
366	    pending: readonly FleetCell[],
367	    spent: number,
368	  ): Promise<void> {
369	    if (pending.length === 0) {
370	      await this.close(session, id, 'completed', 0)
371	      return
372	    }
373	    const remaining = plan.tokenCeiling === undefined ? undefined : plan.tokenCeiling - spent
374	    if (remaining !== undefined && remaining < 1) {
375	      await this.close(session, id, 'ceiling', 0)
376	      return
377	    }
378	    const controller = new AbortController()
379	    this.controller = controller
380	    let ceilingReached = false
381	    // The fleet announces a cell after its session is durable and its
382	    // workspace reaped, so the ledger entry only ever follows the fact.
383	    const unobserve = this.ctx.on('fleet/cell', (payload) => {
384	      if (payload.group !== id) return
385	      if (payload.outcome.kind === 'error' && payload.outcome.code === 'FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED') ceilingReached = true
386	      session.append('shift/cell', {
387	        shiftId: id,
388	        cell: payload.cell,
389	        ...payload.outcome.kind === 'reported' ? { sessionId: payload.outcome.sessionId } : {},
390	        outcome: payload.outcome.kind === 'reported'
391	          ? { kind: 'reported', certified: payload.outcome.certified }
392	          : { kind: 'error', ...payload.outcome.code === undefined ? {} : { code: payload.outcome.code }, message: payload.outcome.message },
393	      })
394	    })
395	    let report: FleetRunReport
396	    try {
397	      report = await this.ctx.fleet.run({
398	        environments: { ids: plan.environments },
399	        models: plan.models,
400	        repetitions: plan.repetitions,
401	        cells: pending,
402	        workspaceRoot: this.config.workspaceRoot,
403	        group: id,
404	        district: plan.district,
405	        ...plan.policyVersion === undefined ? {} : { policyVersion: plan.policyVersion },
406	        ...plan.seed === undefined ? {} : { seed: plan.seed },
407	        ...remaining === undefined ? {} : { tokenCeiling: remaining },
408	        signal: controller.signal,
409	      })
410	    } finally {
411	      unobserve()
412	      this.controller = undefined
413	    }
414	    const outcome = endOutcome(controller.signal.aborted, ceilingReached)
415	    await this.close(session, id, outcome, report.spend.inputTokens + report.spend.outputTokens)
416	  }
417	
418	  /** Append the closing record over every cell the session holds and flush it. */
419	  private async close(session: Session, id: string, outcome: ShiftEndOutcome, spend: number): Promise<void> {
420	    const records = session.events.flatMap(event => (event.type === 'shift/cell' ? [event.data] : []))
421	    session.append('shift/end', { shiftId: id, outcome, spend, cells: countCells(records) })
422	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
423	  }
424	
425	  /**
426	   * Publish one slot session for the length of the slot, flush it, and detach.
427	   * The entry is owned by this fiber, so a disposal that races a slot removes
428	   * it after {@link ShiftService.stop} has let the slot settle.
429	   */
430	  private async publish(session: Session, body: () => Promise<void> | void): Promise<void> {
431	    const detach = this.ctx.effect(function* (this: ShiftService) {
432	      yield this.ctx.sessions.enter(session)
433	      this.ctx.sessions.announce(session)
434	    }.bind(this), `shifts.slot(${session.id})`)
435	    try {
436	      await body()
437	    } finally {
438	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
439	      await detach()
440	    }
441	  }
442	
443	  /** Read every persisted session once: the shift ledgers and the grouped run stamps. */
444	  private async scan(): Promise<ShiftScan> {
445	    const ledgers: ShiftLedger[] = []
446	    const stamped: StampedCell[] = []
447	    for (const header of await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()) {
448	      const inspection = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect(header.id)
449	      const scanned = { meta: inspection.meta, events: inspection.events }
450	      const ledger = foldShiftLedger(scanned)
451	      if (ledger !== undefined) ledgers.push(ledger)
452	      stamped.push(...stampedCells(scanned, foldBudgetSpend(inspection.events, {}).totalTokens))
453	    }
454	    return { ledgers, stamped }
455	  }
456	
457	  /** Resolve one district's environment selection against the registry and freeze its plan. */
458	  private freeze(district: ShiftDistrictConfig): ShiftPlan {
459	    const environments = this.select(district.district, district.plan.environments)
460	    if (environments.length === 0) {
461	      throw new ShiftError(`district "${district.district}" selects no environment`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')
462	    }
463	    return {
464	      district: district.district,
465	      environments,
466	      models: district.plan.models,
467	      repetitions: district.plan.repetitions,
468	      ...district.plan.policyVersion === undefined ? {} : { policyVersion: district.plan.policyVersion },
469	      ...district.plan.seed === undefined ? {} : { seed: district.plan.seed },
470	      ...district.plan.tokenCeiling === undefined ? {} : { tokenCeiling: district.plan.tokenCeiling },
471	    }
472	  }
473	
474	  /** The environment ids one selection names, in registry order for a filter. */
475	  private select(district: string, selection: FleetEnvironmentSelection): EnvironmentId[] {
476	    // The fleet declares the registry injection this driver reads through; a
477	    // composition without it cannot run a cell at all.
478	    const registry = this.ctx.get('environments')
479	    if (registry === undefined) {
480	      throw new ShiftError(`district "${district}" cannot freeze a plan without the environment registry`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')
481	    }
482	    if ('ids' in selection) {
483	      return selection.ids.map((id) => {
484	        if (registry.get(id) === undefined) {
485	          throw new ShiftError(`environment "${id}" of district "${district}" is not registered`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')
486	        }
487	        return id
488	      })
489	    }
490	    return registry.list(selection.filter).map(definition => definition.id)
491	  }
492	}

495	function isDirectory(path: string): boolean {

498	  } catch {
499	    // statSync throws for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the
500	    // deployment named no usable workspace root.
501	    return false
502	  }
503	}

.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-w3-feed-fields.zh.md:9:[Daliesk Village note](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md) 的 rollout 第 8 项点名了 Proving Ground 在喂给强化学习步骤之前需要的四样东西：stamp 上的 `policyVersion` 与 `seed`、轨迹 fold 中被掩码的终止原因、针对 held-out 套件的近重复准入，以及预算策略里的设备槽位资源。第一项和第三项卡在 harness 尚不具备的词汇上。`LlmCallConfig` 里没有任何东西能钉住采样种子，因此一组 rollout 无法陈述它是用什么采样的，同一个重复序号的两个 cell 在构造上就不可比。`EnvironmentRunStamp` 上没有任何字段点名某条路由所服务的检查点，因此 W1 阶段 2 与 W3 阶段 2、9 所读的 `EnvironmentStats` fold 无法按策略版本给测得的难度建键——这正是 [J3 在评审中点出的缺口](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md#council-review)。而环境注册表接受生产者声明的任何 prompt，于是一个合成出来的训练环境可能复述某个 held-out 环境，悄悄污染由该划分算出的每一个数字。
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md:17:Daliesk Village 是一组既有插件按班次运行的组合，绝不是持有日志之外状态的编排脚本。它有三个区写入同一份会话日志：*Workshop*（W2，编译为隐藏标准的客户形态目标，由各程序的账本定节奏）、*Proving Ground*（W1 与 W3，由每条获许可的模型路由作为 fleet cell 运行的环境套件，按策略版本给出 pass@k），以及 *Commons*（W4，keep-or-retire 之下的部门技能与晋升进 fleet 的冻结实验）。每个区都是一份 `cordis.yml` 加一个计划；每个会话都由运行器盖章；观测台展示的每个数字都经由 scorekeeper 从持久化日志折叠而来。
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md:25:- **节奏跟随区。** 每周冻结的 `SuitePlan` 为 Proving Ground 与 Commons 各层定节奏；Workshop 的目标依程序账本与计划关键路径开启与关闭，绝不依日历。
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md:46:第一个班次是一个受 NDA 约束、只读的 Proving Ground 快照，只由已落地的 seam 构成：开放权重路由，每条路由一份 `cordis.yml`，组合环境、`isolation: none` 的运行器、小并发的 fleet、按其价格表设置每会话上限的预算策略、带检查点策略的持久化、scorekeeper 与轨迹导出器；没有 Workshop 会话，没有能外联的工具，每个已盖章却未运行的 cell 都显示为错误行，只有开放权重路由以真名出现，没有成本声明，每一行都带 `tamper: not instrumented`。主机级监督进程重启死掉的班次驱动器，并有一位具名的人为目前还没有任何机制能捕捉的五种情况值班：崩溃的编排器、超出重试预算的整条路由供应商故障、未回收工作区导致的磁盘占满、死掉的班次定时器，以及挂起的工具调用。一个组合门禁（`verify-village-composition`，与 `verify-cordis-config` 并列）拒绝省略预算策略或持久化的区组合，或在没有 monitor 的情况下组合了能外联的工具的区组合。
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md:54:Proving Ground 本身已经是 W3 的 rollout 机制；常驻运行增加的是从 Workshop 失败中持续挖掘环境、持续重新校准 `EnvironmentStats`、为 SFT 冷启动提供稳定的已认证轨迹供给，以及一个公开排行榜，而不是更好的 GRPO 组。在 Proving Ground 供给强化学习步骤之前，stamp 新增 `policyVersion` 与 `seed`，轨迹折叠对被截断、被中止与供应商错误的会话给出 `outcome: null` 而不是 `0`，环境准入新增对留出套件的近重复检查，预算策略新增设备槽位资源，使共享 GPU 上的 rollout 与训练不会悄然互相拖累。AI Village 数据集只在限定为评估用途的数据使用条款下进入：作为 `SessionDiagnosis` 的行为分类法，以及作为用虚构实体重新合成的环境原料，绝不作为训练数据，也绝不作为逐字摘录。[`@deepseek-ai/dsh-curator`](../../../../packages/governance/curator/README.md) 正是让这成为屏障而非声称的东西：策展导出在没有脱敏配置时拒绝运行，并扣留其被钉定的 `dataUse/terms` 不接纳本次导出用途的每一个会话——包括完全不携带条款的会话——于是为评估而接纳的转录从不到达训练导出。

.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md:100:1. **零号班次（Proving Ground，NDA）。** 已落地：`environment/run` stamp 上的 `district`，连同导出器的 `withheldDistricts` 与按请求的 `districts`；fleet 按路由的熔断器（`FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN`）；其计划级 `tokenCeiling` 与整次运行的 `spend`（`FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED`）；其 `workspaceRetention`；组合门禁；预算策略携带价格表摘要的 `usage/priced` 事件；证书上的 executor（读取屏障切片 4）；scorekeeper 把 `usage/priced` 折叠为每次会话的成本与每个已认证会话的成本；以及 stamp 的 `district` 作为观测台据以扣留的 `ScoreboardRow` 键的一部分。仍需要：有人值班运行。
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-w3-feed-fields.md:9:Rollout item 8 of the [Daliesk Village note](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md) names four things the Proving Ground needs before it feeds a reinforcement-learning step: `policyVersion` and `seed` on the stamp, masked terminal reasons in the trajectory fold, near-duplicate admission against the held-out suite, and a device-slot resource in the budget policy. The first and third are blocked on vocabulary the harness does not have. Nothing in `LlmCallConfig` can pin a sampling seed, so a group of rollouts cannot state what it sampled with and two cells of one repetition index are not comparable by construction. Nothing on `EnvironmentRunStamp` names the checkpoint a route served, so the `EnvironmentStats` fold that W1 stage 2 and W3 stages 2 and 9 read cannot key measured difficulty by policy version — the gap [J3 named in the council review](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md#council-review). And the environment registry admits any prompt a producer declares, so a synthesized training environment may restate a held-out one and quietly contaminate every number computed from the split.
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md:17:The Daliesk Village is a composition of existing plugins run in shifts, never an orchestration script that holds state the log does not. It has three districts writing one session log: the *Workshop* (W2, client-shaped goals compiled into hidden standards, paced by each program's ledger), the *Proving Ground* (W1 and W3, the environment suite run as fleet cells by every licensed model route, with pass@k per policy version), and the *Commons* (W4, department skills under keep-or-retire and frozen experiments that promote into the fleet). Every district is a `cordis.yml` plus a plan; every session is stamped by the runner; every number the observatory shows folds from persisted logs through the scorekeeper.
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md:25:- **Cadence follows the district.** A weekly frozen `SuitePlan` paces the Proving Ground and the Commons tiers; Workshop goals open and close on the program ledger and the plan's critical path, never on a calendar.
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md:46:The first shift is an NDA-gated, read-only Proving Ground snapshot built only from landed seams: open-weight routes, one `cordis.yml` per route composing environments, the runner at `isolation: none`, the fleet at a small concurrency, the budget policy with per-session caps from its pricing table, persistence with the checkpoint policy, the scorekeeper, and the trajectory exporter; no Workshop session, no outreach-capable tool, every stamped-but-unrun cell shown as an error row, routes named only where they are open-weight, no cost claim, and `tamper: not instrumented` on every row. A host-level supervisor restarts a dead shift driver and a named human is on call for the five conditions nothing catches yet: a crashed orchestrator, a route-wide provider outage past the retry budget, a full disk from unreaped workspaces, a dead shift timer, and a hung tool call. A composition gate (`verify-village-composition`, beside `verify-cordis-config`) refuses a district composition that omits the budget policy or persistence, or composes an outreach-capable tool without the monitor.
.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md:54:The Proving Ground already is W3's rollout mechanism; always-on operation adds continuous environment mining from Workshop failures, continuous recalibration of `EnvironmentStats`, a standing supply of certified trajectories for the SFT cold start, and a public leaderboard, not better GRPO groups. Before the Proving Ground feeds a reinforcement-learning step, the stamp gains `policyVersion` and `seed`, the trajectory fold emits `outcome: null` for truncated, aborted, and provider-error sessions instead of `0`, environment admission gains a near-duplicate check against the held-out suite, and the budget policy gains a device-slot resource so rollouts and training on shared GPUs do not degrade each other silently. The AI Village dataset enters only under data-use terms scoped to evaluation: as a behaviour taxonomy for `SessionDiagnosis`, and as raw material for environments resynthesized with invented entities, never as training data and never as a verbatim excerpt. [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-curator`](../../../../packages/governance/curator/README.md) is what makes that a barrier rather than a claim: the curated export refuses to run without a redaction profile, and it withholds every session whose pinned `dataUse/terms` do not admit the export's purpose — including every session carrying no terms at all — so a transcript admitted for evaluation never reaches a training export.

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

318	async function harness(scenario: Scenario = {}): Promise<Harness> {
319	  const ctx = new Context()
320	  for (const stub of [StubEnvironments, StubDefaultModel, StubAgents, StubGoals, StubStandards, StubShell, StubSessions]) {
321	    await ctx.plugin(stub)
322	  }
323	  let barrierRoot: string | undefined
324	  if (scenario.barrierPrefix !== undefined) {
325	    await ctx.plugin(StubReadBarrier)
326	    barrierRoot = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), scenario.barrierPrefix))
327	    StubReadBarrier.current.root = barrierRoot
328	  }
329	  await ctx.plugin(EnvironmentRunner, { isolation: 'process', ...scenario.config })
330	  const definition = scenario.definition ?? environment()
331	  StubEnvironments.current.definitions.set(definition.id, definition)
332	  StubAgents.current.agent = new FakeAgent('environment-test', scenario.onTurn ?? assistantTurns)
333	  const workspace = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'environment-runner-'))
334	  const run = (extra: object = {}) => ctx.environmentRuns.run({ environment: definition.id, workspace, ...extra })
335	  return { ctx, workspace, barrierRoot, run }
336	}
